items.title: Investigation and Analysis of the Age-Friendly Dilemma of Smart Elderly Care Services under AI Empowerment
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of population aging and the widespread adoption of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into home- and community-based eldercare. However, many older adults continue to face a digital divide, while smart eldercare products often provide only superficial age-friendly adaptations and fail to match users' needs. This study examines older residents of urban communities and their family members. Drawing on a literature review, a questionnaire survey, and semi-structured interviews, it investigates the development of AI-enabled smart eldercare services and the difficulties older adults encounter when using smart devices and related services. Informed by digital divide theory, active aging theory, and supply-and-demand matching theory, the study analyzes the factors underlying these difficulties and proposes a smart eldercare service model that uses age-friendly short videos as a delivery medium and intergenerational collaboration as its core mechanism. It further develops operational strategies across six dimensions: content, target groups, channels, technology, implementation, and operations. Survey findings are used to assess the model's feasibility. The proposed approach offers communities and social organizations a low-cost, practical framework for more inclusive smart eldercare services, with the aim of narrowing the digital divide and supporting active aging.

items.title: ISLAMIC ETHICS AND THE CRISIS OF DIGITAL INTEGRITY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF TRUTH, DECEPTION AND RESPONSIBILITY IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can now produce fluent text, realistic images and convincing audio at almost no cost, and it does so without any commitment to truth. This has created a crisis of digital integrity: fabricated content is hard to distinguish from authentic content, machine outputs present invented claims as fact, and it is unclear who should answer for the resulting harm. Mainstream AI ethics has responded with principles such as transparency and accountability, but these frameworks draw mainly on Western philosophical traditions and treat deception largely as a technical or regulatory problem. Islamic scholarship on AI has grown quickly, yet most of it addresses AI in general through maqasid al-shariah, and its treatment of misinformation relies almost entirely on the receiver's duty of tabayyun (verification). This concept paper critically analyses truth, deception and responsibility in generative AI through Islamic ethics. Using conceptual analysis and theory adaptation, it synthesises the empirical literature on synthetic media with Qur'anic, prophetic and juristic concepts. It argues that Islamic ethics offers an integrated account built on three pillars: sidq (truthfulness) as a duty owed by every speaker and publisher, the prohibition of ghish, tadlis and kadhib (deception, concealment and falsehood) as limits on design and deployment, and amanah and mas'uliyyah (trust and answerability) as a model of responsibility that always returns to a human agent. The paper proposes a Digital Integrity Framework that distributes these duties across developers, deployers, users and regulators, and offers suggestions for policy, education and future research.

items.title: Judgment in AI Policy Advice: Humans-in-the-Loop, Appreciation, and the DOGE Experience
items.abstract: Recent studies of Policy Advisory Systems (PAS) focus on the quality of advice and how it is designed and managed. This article extends this analysis looking at the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on advisory systems’ behaviour and activity using Geoffrey Vickers’ concept of policy judgment. It notes how negligible user costs combined with the apparent robustness of AI computational outputs can generate advice that can exercise an important and independent influence on policy decisions and outcomes, despite that advice not always being accurate or well-considered. In this sense AI-generated advice shares some of the same characteristics of earlier mechanical algorithms framing policy problems and recommendations for action which lack the hallmarks of careful appreciation of the issues at stake. This is illustrated by the use of AI tools by the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in 2025-2026, in particular its directive to autonomously reduce the number and size of contracts and grants made by many Departments, and specifically the US Department of Veterans Affairs. The case underlines that a crucial design challenge for AI-based policy advice is to go beyond only trying to ensure human oversight or a ‘Human-in-the-Loop’ in order to ensure that problems are properly articulated and actions towards them are sound.

items.title: Kemampuan Berpikir Kritis Generasi Z di Era Artificial Intelligence dan Media Sosial: Perspektif Teori Paulo Freire
items.abstract: The presence of artificial intelligence (AI) and social media has transformed Generation Z’s patterns of learning, information seeking, and everyday interaction. However, previous research findings have not yielded consistent conclusions regarding the effects of these two technologies on critical thinking skills, while studies interpreting them through Paulo Freire’s critical education perspective remain limited. This study aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of AI use and social media use intensity on Generation Z’s critical thinking skills and to interpret the results from Paulo Freire’s perspective. The study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory survey design involving 100 Generation Z respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire and analyzed through multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS. The findings indicate that AI use had no significant partial effect on critical thinking skills (p = 0.416), nor did the intensity of social media use (p = 0.198). Simultaneously, the two variables also had no significant effect on critical thinking skills (p = 0.435) and explained only 1.7% of the variation in these skills (R² = 0.017). These findings are consistent with Paulo Freire’s thought, which positions dialogue, reflection, and praxis as the primary elements in developing critical thinking skills rather than technology alone. This study concludes that AI and social media are not direct determinants of critical thinking skills but rather learning tools whose benefits depend on how users utilize, evaluate, and reflect on information. Theoretically, this study enriches educational research in the digital era by integrating Freire’s critical education perspective. Practically, these findings emphasize the importance of reflective learning, information verification, and dialogical methods in developing Generation Z’s critical thinking skills.

EN This thesis examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of applying artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technologies to the assessment of customers' creditworthiness in commercial bank lending activities. The predictive performance of traditional scoring models (Logistic Regression) and modern AI algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Neural Networks) is comparatively analyzed using ROC-AUC and Gini indicators. The thesis also discusses the use of alternative Big Data sources, the processing of transactional and textual data, and Explainable AI (XAI) and SHAP approaches aimed at mitigating the "black box" problem of artificial intelligence. Based on the findings, practical recommendations are proposed for introducing AI-based credit scoring mechanisms into the national banking system. items.title: Leadership Practices and Employee Motivation of Selected Tenant General Contractors in a Medium-Scale Commercial Project: Basis for a Workforce Engagement Program
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between leadership practices and employee motivation among construction workers employed by selected tenant general contractors in a medium-scale commercial project in Santa Rosa, Laguna, Philippines, as a basis for developing a Workforce Engagement Program. Anchored in Full-Range Leadership Theory and Self-Determination Theory, the study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design involving 63 construction workers from five tenant general contractors selected through total enumeration. Data were collected using an expert-validated structured survey questionnaire and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and Pearson product-moment correlation. Findings revealed that most respondents had limited construction experience and relatively short company tenure. Leadership practices were generally perceived positively, with supervisory support receiving the highest weighted mean (3.76), while recognition and appreciation received the lowest (2.82), indicating weaknesses in formal monetary and non-monetary recognition. Employee motivation was generally high, particularly intrinsic motivation (3.72), followed by professional growth (3.58) and extrinsic motivation (3.57). However, the relationship between leadership practices and employee motivation was statistically nonsignificant (r = −0.022, p = 0.864). The study proposed KILOS-KAPWA: A Construction Workforce Engagement and Recognition Program to strengthen supervisory communication, employee recognition, professional development, workplace support, and participatory decision-making. The findings align with Sustainable Development Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and Sustainable Development Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure). The proposed program may contribute to organizational and socioeconomic sustainability by supporting workforce engagement, employee development, and responsible construction workforce management, although its effectiveness requires evaluation following implementation.

items.title: Local Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Multi-Strategy LLM Prompt Benchmarking with Alignment Verification, and Real-Time Ocular Microsleep Detection
items.abstract: Deploying generative artificial intelligence and deep computer vision architectures into production environments requires overcoming strict hardware memory ceilings, cloud API rate throttling, structural output hallucinations, and real-time latency bounds. This paper presents a unified empirical study of three production-grade artificial intelligence systems engineered specifically for resource-constrained execution across local workstations, cloud-hybrid inference pipelines, and edge vision monitors: (1) A privacy-first, local multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture utilizing 384-dimensional sentence transformers dense embeddings indexed inside an embedded sqlite-vec engine, a dual-layer visual inference router failing over automatically from cloud Qwen 27B (via the Featherless API) to a locally hosted Moondream vision-language model, and a memory-bounded local phi3 inference engine via Ollama constrained to a strict 4,096-token context ceiling to guarantee a 0% out-of-memory (OOM) crash rate; (2) An end-to-end Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation, post-training alignment via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and feedback intelligence framework benchmarking Aspect-Based, Few-Shot, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategies to achieve 99.5% classification accuracy and a 90% reduction in end-to-end processing latency, sustained by a stateful Dynamic API Key Rotation middleware that bypasses the 15 Requests-Per-Minute (15 RPM) free-tier Google Gemini API rate ceiling, alongside deterministic JSON tool-calling schema verification and multimodal reasoning fine-tuning on VEO-3 and Gemini; and (3) A real-time computer vision safety and industrial inspection suite comprising a hybrid ResNet-50 and dlib Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) ensemble for driver microsleep detection (achieving 92% classification accuracy, 35% fewer false positive alerts, and strictly < 100 ms per-frame inference latency across 10,000+ video frames) paired with an OpenCV and TensorFlow-Keras Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictive maintenance pipeline for micro-tool wear classification across 5,000+ augmented images (expanded 100× from 50+ base microscopy images) and 100+ milling intervals using 3 extracted morphological wear descriptors (achieving 75% multi-class classification accuracy).

items.title: LONG-ACTING INJECTABLES DRUG DELIVERY LINKING RELEASE MECHANISMS, PLATFORM DESIGN AND THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Long-acting injectables (LAIs) are innovative drug-delivery systems allowing for prolonged controlled release of a drug after a single administration. By decreasing the dosing frequency, long-acting injectable can have a positive impact on treatment compliance, patient convenience, and drug exposure while minimising the peak–trough fluctuations. This review provides an overview of the different formulation approaches used to develop LAIs, including microspheres, Nano crystal suspensions, oil-based depots, in situ forming depots, implants, hydrogels, lyotropic liquid crystalline systems, polymer-lipid hybrids, and modified protein and peptide therapeutics. The review highlights the main advantages and limitations of LAIs, such as patient adherence and consistent drug exposure, while also discussing injection site reactions, prolonged drug exposure, challenges of flexible dose adjustment, manufacturing complexity, and cost. Storage requirements will be discussed. The clinical applications in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, HIV treatment and prevention, opioid use disorder, growth hormone deficiency, and diabetes. Ophthalmic diseases will be highlighted together with the marketed products in each therapeutic area. Finally, emerging technologies, patient-friendly LAI approaches, biomaterials, artificial intelligence, predictive modelling, and personalised medicine are discussed. In conclusion, LAIs are an important class of drug delivery systems that can have a significant impact on optimal and sustained drug exposure while decreasing the treatment burden on the patient. The complexity of the different formulation approaches and the need for clinical development expertise are still major hurdles that industry is currently trying to address by developing new approaches and manufacturing processes.

items.title: Looking Beyond the Grade: Do Academic Performance and Motivations Predict Attachment in Close Relationships?
items.abstract: The ability to form healthy attachments with others has long been established to be important for mental health and well-being. The Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised Scale (Fraley et al., 2000) identifies two dimensions of attachment - model of self (attachment anxiety; degree to which an individual worries about rejection, abandonment, or unworthiness of love), and model of other (attachment avoidance; degree to which an individual fears emotional intimacy, suppresses dependency, and insists upon behavioral self-reliance). However, less is understood about whether the impact of attachment spills over in the academic lives of college students. The current study examines whether academic performance (GPA) and/or academic motivation (subscales in the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire; Pintrich et al., 1991) is predictive of attachment in college students (N = 112). Separate multiple linear regression analyses will be conducted to examine if GPA and/or subscales of academic motivation (intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, task value, control of learning beliefs, self-efficacy for learning and performance, and test anxiety) can predict attachment (model of self and model of other). Understanding whether academic performance and/or academic motivation is predictive of attachment styles is fundamental to understanding the value of social connections in academic settings. Such insights can aid institutions in tailoring guidance to help students reach their full academic potential. Keywords: attachment styles, academic performance, academic motivation

items.title: Machine Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Predicting 10-Year Mortality after Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is associated with short-term outcomes after cardiac surgery, but its value for long-term mortality prediction remains unclear. We developed a machine learning model incorporating NLR to predict 10-year all-cause mortality after cardiac surgery, and used explainable artificial intelligence to interpret the role of NLR. Methods We included adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from the MIMIC-IV database. The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Six machine learning models were compared using grid search, stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap internal validation. The best model was interpreted using SHAP on the test set. The NLR cutoff was identified by piecewise regression on the training set. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. Results Among 4,891 patients (median age 68 years), 222 (4.54%) died within 10 years. After tuning, XGBoost performed best (optimism-corrected AUC = 0.815; 95% CI: 0.758–0.861), outperforming LASSO regression (AUC = 0.780). NLR alone had an AUC of 0.709, similar to APACHE III (0.732; P = 0.630). Combining NLR with APACHE III improved the AUC to 0.761 (P = 0.002). SHAP analysis identified APACHE III (0.371) and NLR (0.291) as the top two predictors. Piecewise regression identified an NLR cutoff of 6.5. At a 15% risk threshold, the positive predictive value was 23.3% (5.1-fold enrichment). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit across thresholds of 5%-30%. Conclusions Preoperative NLR is an independent predictor of 10-year mortality after cardiac surgery, with performance comparable to APACHE III. The tuned XGBoost model showed good overall performance. An NLR threshold of 6.5 was identified and supported by SHAP analysis. NLR may complement existing risk scores for long-term risk stratification, but should not be used as a standalone tool.

items.abstract: Teacher human resource quality improvement management is an important aspect of efforts to improve the quality of education in schools. This study aims to analyze teacher human resource quality improvement management in improving the quality of education at SMA Negeri 1 Pamekasan. This study used a descriptive qualitative approach involving the principal, vice principal for curriculum affairs, teachers, and school documentation as data sources. Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, then analyzed through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data validity was confirmed through source triangulation and technique triangulation. The results show that teacher quality improvement was carried out through needs-based planning by utilizing SWOT analysis and the education report card, as well as the implementation of various development programs, such as In-House Training (IHT), MGMP, supervision, technology training, and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in learning. Teacher quality improvement contributed to more active learning, increased student creativity and achievement, and improved school education report card results. However, its implementation still faced challenges in the form of technological adaptation and resistance to change among senior teachers. This study contributes to the development of educational human resource management studies, particularly in strengthening teacher quality as a strategic factor in improving school quality. The implications of this study emphasize the importance of teacher development planning that is needs-based, sustainable, and responsive to the transformation of learning technology.

items.title: Mapping Artificial Intelligence Research in Strategic Management: A Bibliometric Analysis and Future Research Agenda
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in strategic decision-making, competitive positioning, innovation management, organizational learning, and governance, yet the literature remains fragmented across management, information systems, innovation, and technology-management fields. This study provides a focused bibliometric review of AI research in strategic management. Scopus was used as the primary database, and the query "artificial intelligence" AND "strategic management" was applied to titles, abstracts, and keywords, with restrictions to Business, Management and Accounting, Article and Review document types, and English-language publications. From 126 retrieved records, relevance screening excluded 82 records, leaving 44 publications for analysis. The study examines annual trends, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, country distribution, science maps, TCCM synthesis, and a WoS/SSCI sensitivity analysis. Results show slow development before 2018 and marked acceleration after 2023, with 2026 treated as an incomplete year. Themes are shifting from decision support and strategic planning toward generative AI, innovation management, sustainability, organizational capabilities, and governance. By combining bibliometric mapping, TCCM, and cross-database sensitivity analysis, this study offers a knowledge-structure map and future research agenda.

items.title: Measuring Artificial Intelligence Integration in South African Private Higher Education: Applying a Refined Academic Quality Management Model
items.abstract: This study applies a refined model of Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into Academic Quality Management Systems (AQMS) within South African private higher education. It builds on prior validation through exploratory factor analysis and reliability testing to examine how institutional factors relate to stakeholders’ perceptions of AI integration. Survey data from higher education and education technology stakeholders were analysed using PLS-SEM, correlation, multiple regression, and descriptive statistics. The results show moderate explanatory power, with regression indicating stronger overall model performance than PLS-SEM. Across analyses, Research Governance and Responsible AI Use emerged as the most consistent and statistically supported factor associated with AI_QMS. Strategic Planning and AI in Teaching and Learning also contributed positively, although their effects varied by method. In contrast, AI Literacy and Competency Development and Assessment and Evaluation produced inconsistent results, including negative regression coefficients, which are interpreted cautiously due to shared variance and measurement limitations. Other factors, including Ethical Considerations and Data Privacy, Environmental Impact, and Interdisciplinary Collaboration, did not demonstrate independent explanatory power in multivariable models. The findings highlight that observable institutional activity does not necessarily translate into consistent integration within academic quality systems. The study contributes a multi-dimensional framework that distinguishes between strongly supported relationships, method-dependent effects, and areas requiring further measurement development. Practically, the model provides institutions with a structured approach to assess and strengthen AI integration within academic quality management.

items.title: Model Degradation: Monitoring Human Activity Recognition with Classical Drift Detectors
items.abstract: This work investigates the impact of data drift on machine learning models deployed for Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using the UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones dataset. A Random Forest classifier is trained on an initial stable data distribution using a chronological split to reflect real-world deployment conditions. Model performance is first evaluated under no-drift conditions to establish a baseline. To study degradation, data drift is simulated by injecting Gaussian noise into the sensor features of future data, representing realistic changes such as sensor noise and calibration shifts. This controlled perturbation leads to a measurable decline in classification accuracy, precision, and recall, demonstrating the vulnerability of static models to evolving data distributions. Model degradation is monitored using the ADWIN (Adaptive Windowing) drift detection algorithm applied to the prediction error stream, enabling automatic identification of statistically significant performance changes. To mitigate degradation, a sliding-window retraining strategy is applied using recent samples, resulting in partial recovery of model performance. The results highlight the importance of time-aware evaluation, drift detection, and lightweight retraining for maintaining reliable machine learning systems in dynamic and resource-constrained environments.

items.title: Motivations and Constraints for Playing Electronic Games: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: The objective of this scoping review was to map the existing scientific literature on the relationship between motivations and constraints for playing digital games and esports, characterizing study profiles, identifying dominant themes and tensions, and examining the extent to which their interaction has been theorized and empirically investigated. Following Arksey and O'Malley’s framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a search across EBSCO, SCOPUS, and Web of Science identified 38 eligible studies published between 1985 and 2025. The findings reveal a profound structural and theoretical imbalance: research is heavily skewed toward motivation-driven "pull factors" (76.3 %), while constraints remain critically understudied (13.2 %). Crucially, integrative studies (10.5 %) demonstrate that while intrinsic motivations can mitigate logistical barriers, deep psychosocial and symbolic constraints rooted in identity exclusion and social stigma consistently override motivation, triggering disengagement or severe affective costs. This review exposes the theoretical limitations of isolated psychological models, arguing for integrative, socio-culturally sensitive frameworks capable of capturing motivations and constraints as interdependent dynamics of the situated gaming experience.

items.title: Multi-dimensional hierarchical temporal alignment for improved temporal commonsense reasoning in large language models
items.abstract: Benefiting from recent advances in generative AI and large language models (LLMs), current LLM-driven AI systems are rapidly reshaping how we reason, plan, and make decisions. Yet endowing these systems with human-like temporal intelligence (e.g., understanding and comparing events across time) remains largely unresolved. To address this gap, we introduce a novel Multi-dimensional Hierarchical Temporal Alignment framework (denoted as MHTA), of which the core idea is to effectively ground the temporal alignment of an LLM in both event-specific and cross-event real-world temporal commonsense knowledge. Specifically, we first frame the temporal space as a multi-dimensional hierarchical space, where each dimension comprises its own set of temporal units. Building on this formulation, we curate an initial burn-in dataset in which annotations are constructed to reflect real-world human temporal commonsense in accordance with our defined temporal space. Based on the initial burn-in dataset, we propose two complementary fine-tuning objectives: (i) Grounding the temporal alignment in event-specific temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved through a novel hierarchy-preserving Wasserstein loss, and (ii) Grounding the temporal alignment in cross-event temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved via a margin-adaptive triplet loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of MHTA, we conduct extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks (MCTACO, DurationQA, and TimeDial). For example, on the MCTACO dataset, MHTA improves Mistral-7B by 6.0% in accuracy and 10.3% in exact match, and improves DeepSeek-LLM-7B by 5.4% in accuracy and 9.8% in exact match. Combined with different backbones, MHTA surpasses nearly all baselines across the three benchmarks and exceeds the performance of advanced models such as GPT-4o on MCTACO and DurationQA. These results demonstrate that MHTA provides consistent gains in temporal commonsense reasoning across diverse LLM backbones.

items.title: Neurocognitive Contributors to Reaching Movement Corrections Following Physical and Visual Perturbations
items.abstract: This study compares how young adults make rapid online reaching corrections following either physical or visual perturbations, and whether cognitive abilities predict corrective motor performance. Sixty-one participants completed an obstacle avoidance reaching task using a robotic interface that introduced either force-based physical perturbations or visually displaced cursor feedback and completed measures of cognitive performance. Behavioral analyses showed that collision rates did not differ between perturbation modalities; however, movement corrections following visual perturbations were significantly slower than those following physical, particularly when participants navigated around obstacles. Participants were also more likely to select outward corrective paths during physical perturbations. Regression analyses demonstrated that processing speed, psychomotor speed, and executive control predicted corrective movement performance, with stronger cognitive associations observed for visual perturbations. These findings suggest that although both perturbation types rely on shared corrective motor processes, responses to visual perturbations require greater cortical and cognitive involvement than responses to physical perturbations.

items.title: NEXT-GENERATION ADVANCEMENTS IN POLYMERIC MICRONEEDLES AND NANO CARRIER-MEDIATED TRANSDERMAL DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS
items.abstract: Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide several advantages over conventional oral and parenteral routes, including avoidance of gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism, improved patient compliance, and controlled drug delivery. However, the stratum corneum acts as a major barrier, limiting the passive transport of hydrophilic and high-molecular-weight therapeutic agents. This review focuses on recent advances in polymeric microneedles and nanocarrier-mediated transdermal drug delivery systems developed to overcome these skin-permeation limitations. Literature from PubMed and Scopus was reviewed with emphasis on microneedle classification, polymeric biomaterials, nanocarrier systems, drug-loading capacity, permeation mechanisms, safety, and clinical translation. Polymeric microneedles, including solid, coated, dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and hollow systems, enable controlled and minimally painful delivery by creating temporary microchannels through the stratum corneum. Nanocarriers such as liposomes, ethosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, polymeric nanoparticles, and inorganic nanoparticles further enhance dermal and transdermal drug transport through lipid fluidization, follicular pathways, and controlled drug deposition. The integration of these technologies provides promising opportunities for delivering macromolecules, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Future developments involving stimuli-responsive systems, wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence, microfluidics, and personalized manufacturing may further enhance transdermal therapy. Despite challenges related to manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, and long-term biocompatibility, advanced microneedle and nanocarrier platforms have considerable potential for clinical translation and personalized drug delivery. Background: Traditional transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide a non-invasive, patient-compliant route that avoids gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism. However, the impermeable lipid matrix of the stratum corneum strictly limits the passive transport of molecules to those possessing specific hydrophobic profiles and low molecular weights. Objective: This comprehensive review examines contemporary physical and chemical breakthrough technologies, with specific focus on polymeric microneedles (MNs) and nanocarrier-facilitated delivery platforms engineered to overcome these macro-molecular transport constraints. Methodology: A systematic screening of literature from the PubMed and Scopus databases (spanning foundational models through 2026) was conducted to evaluate the mechanical structural properties, biopolymer selections, and systemic pharmacokinetics of advanced skin-permeation platforms. Results: Polymeric microneedles (dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and stimuli-responsive types) demonstrate precise disruption of the stratum corneum without contacting dermally located pain-sensitive nerve endings. Concurrently, lipidic, polymeric, and inorganic nanocarriers capitalize on hair follicles and transient lipid fluidization to deposit high-molecular-weight biologics, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Conclusion: Combining active mechanical microneedles with target-specific nanocarriers represents the vanguard of modern personalized diagnostics and therapeutics, bridging laboratory innovation with clinical scale-up paradigms.

items.title: Novokult LLM: On the New Culture
items.abstract: Novokult LLM is a desktop application that runs a large language model on your own computer. It is built for left-wing organizers, researchers, and writers. Once a model file is on your machine, drafting, analysis, and chat can stay there. It has three modes: analysis of events and texts through a Marxist framework, agitprop drafting (leaflets, slogans, speeches, songs, strike bulletins), and free chat. You can load your own texts as a Sources Library, turn on web search routed through Tor, and export posters. The design starts from an argument. AI is machinery, and most of it is rented from a few firms that see every prompt. Novokult runs the machine where its users live and work, and its code is published under the Peer Production License, a copyfarleft license meant to keep it in common. The title of this paper names the older question behind that choice: who builds a movement's culture, and with what tools. The name Novokult contracts the Russian новая культура (novaya kultura), "new culture." Version 1.0.0 is built for Windows (portable and installer) and Linux (AppImage and deb). An Android port exists in the code but is unfinished.

items.title: Occupational Airborne Pollutant Exposure and Hematological Outcomes in Workplace Settings: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Occupational exposure to airborne pollutants poses a significant risk to hematological health. This systematic review aims to evaluate the associations between workplace airborne pollutants and key blood parameters, as well as the modifying roles of age and body mass index (BMI) among adult industrial workers. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search across Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Medline identified studies published over the last five decades. The search strategy incorporated terms related to occupational air pollution and airborne pollutants, including particulate matter (PM), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and heavy metals (HMs). Studies evaluating occupational exposures and reporting hematological outcomes-hemoglobin concentration, mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH), mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), and anemia prevalence-were included. Methodological quality was assessed using study design-specific JBI critical appraisal checklists. Out of 1855 retrieved records, 55 studies (predominantly from developing and industrializing countries) met the eligibility criteria. Findings reveal that workplace exposure to VOCs, HMs (e.g., lead), and PM is consistently associated with subclinical hematological alterations, characterized by lower hemoglobin levels and altered red blood cell indices (MCH and MCHC). Notably, despite high workplace pollutant concentrations, linear correlations between pollutant levels and hematological indices were often weak, indicating complex exposure-response dynamics. Analysis of modifying factors showed that higher BMI was positively associated with hemoglobin levels, potentially suggesting a protective buffering pattern, whereas age exhibited weak associations, likely reflecting a "healthy-worker effect" in exposed populations. The complexity of these findings underscores the necessity of moving beyond single-pollutant assessments toward evaluating mixed workplace exposures. Integrating routine hematological surveillance and nutritional screening into occupational health programs is crucial for mitigating workplace hematotoxicity.

EN This article examines the theoretical-methodological, technological, and practical aspects of the digital transformation of higher education at the current stage. It highlights promising directions for creating digital ecosystems in higher education institutions and integrating information management systems (HEMIS, LMS), artificial intelligence (AI), adaptive learning technologies, and Big Data into the educational process. The article also analyzes key systemic issues arising in the digitalization process, including the digital divide, the need to develop the digital pedagogical competencies of academic staff, and cybersecurity risks. items.title: On a conjecture of Sun on sums of four numbers x(5x±1)/2
items.abstract: Z.-W. Sun conjectured (arXiv:2411.14308, Conjecture 5.5) that every integer n > 51 can be written as w(5w−1)/2 + x(5x−1)/2 + y(5y+1)/2 + z(5z+1)/2 with w, x, y, z natural numbers. We prove the stronger statement that every natural number n except n = 1 and n = 19 has such a representation. The problem reduces to finding lattice points on a sphere in a coset of 10Z⁴ with exactly two negative coordinates. We detect these with a degree-8 polynomial weight, and bound the resulting theta series of weights 2 to 10 and level 400 through explicit newform decompositions and Deligne's bound. This leaves 8,167,125 explicit integers below 10¹⁰, which are checked directly. The proof is computer-assisted: the decompositions are certified in ball arithmetic and the polynomial inequality in exact arithmetic. An independent audit by a separate AI run recomputed every step with different code and found no error. All modular-forms constants were also re-derived independently in SageMath, without PARI/GP, and every constant matched. An external review by ChatGPT found no objection to the main proof; its wording points have been corrected. No human expert has yet checked the argument. The mathematics, code and audits were produced by the AI system Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction; see Section 8 of the paper. This record contains the paper, all programs, certificates, logs and the audit report.

items.title: On the Issue of International Legal Guarantees for Personal Data Protection in the Context of Hybrid Warfare
items.abstract: This article investigates the complex problem of protecting human personal data during modern armed conflicts, particularly through the prism of hybrid warfare. The rapid pace of digitalization, the advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, and their active integration into the military sphere drive the relevance of this study. These factors cause fundamental changes in the methods and means of warfare, as well as in the very purpose of armed conflict. Today, informational influence and psychological pressure on the enemy's population - which are not always accompanied by a direct armed attack - constitute an integral component of any 21st-century military conflict. Consequently, the study analyzes the concept of hybrid warfare, defining it through characteristic features such as asymmetry, large-scale involvement of non-state actors, latency, and a combination of military and non-military means of struggle. The research specifically focuses on the role of generative artificial intelligence in the context of growing cyber threats. The paper emphasizes that unauthorized access to individuals' personal data during an armed conflict allows opposing parties to exert targeted psychological influence on population groups or individuals, manipulate public opinion through disinformation and «deepfakes,» and apply illegal filtration and terror against the population. Furthermore, this study analyzes the current international legal framework regarding personal data protection in conflict conditions. It examines the provisions of international humanitarian law, particularly the Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949. The findings establish that IHL norms lack special provisions for protecting digitized information. Moreover, ongoing discussions among researchers regarding the recognition of digital data as a «civilian object» significantly complicate the qualification of an enemy's actions in cyberspace as a violation of international humanitarian law. Finally, the article explores the provisions of specific international acts regulating data protection. The analysis determines that the permitted derogation from certain obligations in this sphere can lead to state abuses, often hidden behind the necessity of ensuring national security and defense. Ultimately, the paper highlights that international human rights law, through the provisions of international treaties and the case law of the ECtHR, establishes general guarantees to ensure compliance with the criteria of legality, strict necessity, and proportionality when interfering with the human right to personal data protection.

items.title: Opinion: Decisions without documents: Records continuity and evidential accountability in agentic supply chains
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence is taking supply chain software from recommendation to execution. Planning and procurement agents now execute replenishment orders, reallocate freight, and negotiate with suppliers based on delegated powers, all without simultaneous human approval. Virtually every organization maintains the records of such activities as log files, subject only to IT retention policies until the files are no longer useful for diagnostic purposes and then disposed of. This opinion article contends that such treatment misclassifies what is, in substance, evidence of business transactions. An agent-executed decision that commits expenditure, alters a contractual position or redistributes risk across trading partners creates obligations that auditors, counterparties, regulators and courts may later test, and its trace therefore meets the functional definition of a record. Drawing on records continuum theory, the article follows a single agent decision across the dimensions of creation, capture, organisation and pluralisation and locates the points at which it leaves any recordkeeping regime. It then specifies the attributes of a trustworthy decision record in terms of reliability, authenticity and integrity, and proposes a governance arrangement in which records and information managers hold design authority over decision records alongside IT, procurement, legal and audit functions. The argument is addressed to information professionals in commercial settings who will increasingly be asked to evidence what an agent did, and on whose authority.

items.title: PaReGTA: a temporally aware LLM-based patient representation framework for EHR analytics
items.abstract: Temporal information in structured electronic health records (EHRs) is often lost in sparse one-hot or count-based representations, while sequence models can be costly and data-hungry. We propose PaReGTA, an LLM-based encoding framework that (i) converts longitudinal EHR events into visit-level templated text with explicit temporal cues, (ii) learns domain-adapted visit embeddings via lightweight contrastive fine-tuning of a sentence-embedding model, and (iii) aggregates visit embeddings into a fixed-dimensional patient representation using hybrid temporal pooling that captures both recency and globally informative visits. The resulting fixed-dimensional patient representations can be used with conventional downstream machine-learning models. To examine factor-level sensitivity, we use PaReGTA-RSS (Representation Shift Score), a prespecified factor-removal analysis that recomputes patient representations after removing clinically defined factor groups and quantifies the resulting change in the fitted logit of a fixed logistic-regression model. We evaluated PaReGTA in a cohort of 39 088 patients with migraine from the All of Us Research Program (AoU) on a retrospective patient-level classification task with an EHR-derived target. In an exploratory comparison on the fixed held-out test cohort of 7818 patients, PaReGTA-Gap + LightGBM, used as a post hoc analytical reference, had the highest reported AUC, accuracy, and F1 values among the evaluated sparse, BERT-based EHR, and recurrent approaches in this cohort.

items.title: Pengaruh Literasi Digital terhadap Etika Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence pada Mahasiswa Perguruan Tinggi
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education has transformed the way students seek information, complete assignments, and understand academic materials. However, AI use also raises ethical issues, including plagiarism, overreliance on instant answers, and a lack of transparency in acknowledging AI assistance. This study aims to analyze the effect of digital literacy on the ethical use of AI among university students. A quantitative survey method was employed. Data were collected using a 1–5 Likert-scale questionnaire from 125 respondents, with 119 complete responses analyzed. Digital literacy was measured using 12 items, while ethical AI use was measured using 12 items. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity testing, reliability testing, correlation, and simple linear regression. The results show that digital literacy has a positive and significant effect on ethical AI use. The correlation coefficient of 0.638 indicates a strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination of 0.406 indicates that digital literacy explains 40.6% of the variation in ethical AI use. The regression equation is Y = 1.196 + 0.706X. These findings indicate that students with higher digital literacy tend to use AI more ethically, responsibly, and transparently. This study recommends strengthening digital literacy programs with an emphasis on AI ethics in higher education.

items.title: Physical activity, emotional intelligence and physical self-concept in Secondary Education teachers: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Teachers’ health and well-being are essential for promoting positive educational environments and healthy lifestyles within schools. Emotional intelligence and physical self-concept have emerged as relevant psychological factors associated with engagement in physical activity; however, evidence among secondary education teachers remains limited. The objective of this study was to analyse the relationships between physical activity, trait emotional intelligence and perceived physical self-concept among secondary education teachers, as well as to examine the indirect association between emotional intelligence and physical activity through physical self-concept. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 85 secondary education teachers from schools in the Region of Murcia (Spain). Participants completed the Trait Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire-Short Form (TEIQue-SF), the Physical Self-Concept Questionnaire (PSQ), and a physical activity assessment based on the PACE questionnaire. Descriptive analyses, Pearson correlations, MANOVA, and structural equation modelling were performed. Physical activity was positively associated with all dimensions of physical self-concept and with the sociability dimension of emotional intelligence. Teachers reporting higher levels of physical activity showed more favourable perceptions of their physical competence, condition, strength and self-esteem. In an exploratory structural equation model, emotional intelligence was positively associated with physical self-concept, which in turn was associated with physical activity; the indirect effect of emotional intelligence on physical activity through physical self-concept was significant (β = .18; 95% bootstrap CI [.03, .42]) and the direct effect was non-significant, a pattern statistically consistent with mediation that requires longitudinal confirmation. Physical activity is associated with better physical self-perceptions and greater emotional resources among secondary education teachers. These findings highlight the potential value of promoting active lifestyles within educational settings as a strategy to enhance teachers’ well-being and occupational health. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the causal relationships among these variables.

items.title: Postgraduate Students' AI Engagement in L2 Academic Writing: Toward Student‐Led Human– AI Collaborations
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the teaching and learning of second language (L2) writing. Despite AI's affordances in assisting L2 writing, improvements in writing skills and learning outcomes that extend beyond producing polished texts largely depend on students' active AI engagement, typically involving AI‐generated content and AI tools. This study adopts a qualitative, classroom‐based inquiry to examine how 56 L2 postgraduate students engage with AI in an authentic academic writing class. Framing engagement as a multidimensional meta‐construct, we identify a contextualized pattern of engagement characterized by students' agential role in shaping human–AI interactions across behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and social dimensions. Specifically, behavioral engagement occurs at compositional and operational levels, whereas cognitive engagement involves cognitive autonomy and metacognitive awareness. Students' emotional engagement involves appreciation and relief, as well as caution and emotional distance. Social engagement intersects with other dimensions, potentially shaping how students act, think, and feel in relation to AI through collaborative reflection. The findings inform a reconceptualization of engagement as a fluid, situated process, moving beyond a simple engagement–disengagement dichotomy toward a dynamic continuum shaped by the ongoing interplay across its multiple dimensions, encompassing both synergies and tensions. Implications for L2 writing and learning are also discussed.

items.title: Practice report on a credit-based internship for Medical Sciences students: Examining educational effects through fundamental skills for working adults and qualitative content analysis.
items.abstract: Objectives: This study examined the educational outcomes of a credit-based internship program for third-year university students majoring in Medical Sciences, focusing on changes in their Fundamental Skills for Working Adults and career awareness. Methods: Participants were 57 third-year students from the Faculty of Medical Sciences at University A enrolled in a credit-based internship course. On completion of the internship, a web-based questionnaire was administered. The survey included self-evaluations of Fundamental Skills for Working Adults, Likert scales to evaluate subjective learning outcomes, and open-ended responses. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were categorized using qualitative content analysis. Results: Forty-two students responded to the questionnaire (response rate: 73.7%). For Fundamental Skills for Working Adults, more than 80% reported improvements in Proactivity, Active Listening, Situational Awareness, and Discipline. Subjective evaluations showed high overall satisfaction, with 97.6% of respondents reporting being either "very satisfied" or "satisfied," and 95.2% reporting changes in future vision and career awareness. Qualitative analysis yielded five categories, including "multifaceted understanding of medical settings and workplaces" and "concretization of career visions." Conclusion: Credit-based internships can effectively contribute to the development of Fundamental Skills for Working Adults and enhance career awareness among Medical Sciences students.

items.title: Predictive PLS-SEM Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Innovative Marketing
items.abstract: Marketing has witnessed a digital transformation driven by the fast evolution of technology and International Intelligence (AI), as businesses can now implement intelligent chatbot systems to boost customer interaction and improve the overall performance of the business. The study explores the relationships between Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Quality, Customer Trust, Perceived Ease of Use, Innovative Marketing Capability, Customer Experience, Supply Chain Integration and Business Performance, applying Predictive Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). A mediation analysis, PLSpredict, and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) were used in SmartPLS 4 to analyse the primary data collected from 526 participants who have previously utilised AI-powered chatbots. The result show that AI Chatbot Quality significantly positively affects Innovative Marketing Capability and Customer Experience, and Customer Trust and Perceived Ease of Use positively influence Customer Experience. Customer Experience positively influences Supply Chain Integration and Business Performance and acts as a mediator between AI Chatbot Quality and Business Performance. The study combines the TAM and RBV models into a single predictive model, offering theoretical perspectives and practical implications for organisations looking to enable their AI chatbots to enhance their innovative marketing efforts and gain a sustainable competitive edge.

items.title: Predictive Threshold Modeling of Evolutionary Plasticity and Colony Collapse Risk in Apis Mellifera Through Climate-Driven Architectural Degradation, BehavioralEnergetics, And Material Economy Using YOLO-Seg, and Sentinel-3 Framework
items.abstract: Abstract Climate-induced change now stands out as a critical driver of how social insects adjust their behavior and build nests - though exactly how temperature links to nest architecture still lacks clear quantification. A method combining artificial intelligence with satellite data helps track niche architectural drift in Apis mellifera , focusing on the degradation of hexagonal comb symmetry when the weather turns unstable. Satellite records from Sentinel-3, along with MODIS and ERA5-Land systems, feed into a detailed climate picture spanning 24 years, stretching back to 1999 and reaching toward 2026. Google Earth Engine processes these inputs across three areas marked by different ecosystems: one in Canada near Prince Albert at 53.13°N and 106.35°W, another in Morocco’s Rabat region located at 33.97°N and 6.84°W, plus a third site situated eastward in Lithuania’s capital zone, Vilnius, around 54.68°N and 25.27°E. To evaluate high-resolution comb images from detailed comb scans, a Symmetry Coefficient (S c ) emerged using YOLOv11-seg for instance segmentation alongside OpenCV-driven symmetry calculations. Instance segmentation mapped each cell position, and the behavior patterns quantification followed through pose estimation models like OpenBeePose and VGG-19. Instead of relying on surface metrics, material flow was assessed via Wax-to-Storage Ratio (WSR), built from 3D reconstructions to evaluate material efficiency. Data point to one clear trend: when heat fluctuation rises, hive structure weakens significantly (β = −0.08495, p < 0.01). Below a critical symmetry threshold, S c value of 0.6214, survival odds drop sharply, with collapse probability reaching 70%. As temperatures climb, information in waggle signals loses coherence; entropy measures expose systemic breakdowns deeper than mere shape changes. By this comparative study, differential phenotypic plasticity is confirmed, which shows how Boreal groups handle change compared to Mediterranean ones - their stability score sits at 0.852, noticeably higher resilience than the 0.665 found southward. The research develops a predictive ecological threshold paradigm that connects behavior, energetics, environmental stress, and structural effects. Instead of just measuring shifts, it builds bridges between machine learning and real-world animal actions amid warming climates. Early warnings for bee network instability become possible through this lens, scaling across regions without losing precision.

items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the "Kajino Multiplicative Language Model (KM-LLM)," a novel computational architecture designed to overcome the fundamental flaws of current Large Language Models (LLMs)—specifically, their reliance on vector addition (\boldsymbol{v}_A + \boldsymbol{v}_B), which leads to contextual collapse, hallucinations, and ideological polarization. KM-LLM shifts the core computational paradigm from additive vector spaces to multiplicative tensor products (\boldsymbol{v}_A \otimes \boldsymbol{v}_B), introducing absolute core-theme invariance (1^n = 1) and an automatic zero-logic circuit breaker (1 \times 1 \times 0 = 0). Furthermore, this paper formalizes the "Societal Dynamics Model" (\text{Society} = \text{Right} \times \text{Left}) to demonstrate the mathematical decay dynamics triggered by values below 1. We prove that while additive models erroneously permit incomplete compromises or unilateral bias, KM-LLM enforces absolute parity (1 \times 1 = 1) and synergistic expansion (> 1) as mandatory mathematical conditions for system stability and societal sustainability.

items.title: Prevalence of hypertension and associated occupational factors among steel and ceramic tile workers in Vietnam
items.abstract: Hypertension is one of the most prevalent non-communicable diseases worldwide and a leading risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Industrial workers, particularly those exposed to unfavorable working conditions and high work intensity, may be at increased risk. However, evidence on hypertension among industrial workers operating under tropical hot and humid conditions remains limited.We aimed to determine the prevalence of hypertension and analyze associated factors among steel workers and ceramic tile workers in Vietnam.A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted in 2022 among 1 228 production workers from two industrial enterprises, including 836 steel workers and 392 ceramic tile workers. Blood pressure was measured using a standardized protocol. Structured interviews were used to collect information on sociodemographic characteristics, working conditions, job stress, smoking, and alcohol consumption. Hypertension was defined according to Vietnamese Ministry of Health guidelines. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and binary analyses to estimate crude odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs).The overall prevalence of hypertension was 22,3%. Ceramic tile workers exhibited a higher prevalence of hypertension (39,8%) compared with steel workers (14,1%) (p < 0.001). Workers aged ≥35 years had a higher likelihood of hypertension than those aged <35 years (OR = 2,2; 95% CI: 1,71–2,95). Similarly, workers with a working duration of ≥10 years were more likely to have hypertension than those with <10 years of employment (OR = 3,6; 95% CI: 2,70–4,85). High proportions of workers reported smoking and harmful alcohol consumption in both occupational groups.Conclusion. Hypertension represents an important occupational health problem among industrial workers in Vietnam, particularly among older workers and those with longer working duration, highlighting the potential role of prolonged exposure to unfavorable working conditions in tropical industrial settings.

Results: A total of 423 university students participated in this study. The prevalence of moderate non-specific low back pain (NPRS 4–6) was found to be 61.7%, while 16.8% of participants demonstrated moderate functional disability (ODI 21–40%). Statistical analysis revealed a significant moderate positive correlation between pain intensity and functional disability (r ≈ 0.31, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Most university students had moderate non-specific low back pain. Higher pain intensity was associated with greater functional disability. items.title: Prevention of Work‐Related Musculoskeletal Disorders and Career Sustainability in Head and Neck Reconstructive Surgery: Integrating Ergonomics and Physical Conditioning
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Head and neck reconstructive and plastic surgery exposes surgeons to prolonged static posture, sustained visualization of a narrow operative field, cervical and shoulder loading, fine-motor work, and extended standing. These demands create a substantial occupational musculoskeletal burden. METHODS: A structured narrative review and expert perspective synthesized evidence from head and neck surgery, reconstructive microsurgery, plastic surgery, surgical ergonomics, occupational health, and rehabilitation. RESULTS: Musculoskeletal symptoms commonly involve the neck, shoulders, back, and upper extremities and often begin during residency. Exposure varies by operative phase, visualization, anthropometric and team-level mismatch, prolonged standing, and repetitive operative workload. Prevention extends beyond ergonomic setup to phase-specific exposure modification, physical conditioning, mobility and recovery, footwear and standing-surface optimization, wearable feedback, early assessment, and diagnosis-specific rehabilitation. CONCLUSIONS: Career sustainability requires reducing avoidable occupational load while preserving physical capacity and restoring function through recognition, modification, conditioning, recovery, assessment, and rehabilitation.

items.abstract: PRIME — Scientific Intelligence is a research and engineering program focused on the development of a verifiable artificial intelligence infrastructure for science, engineering, and technological innovation. This technical report documents the development of the PRIME program between 6 August and 29 October 2026, including scientific data infrastructure, continued pre-training campaigns, scientific simulation and verification systems, PSSF-v2, AiiDA workflow orchestration, sealed benchmarks, reproducibility mechanisms, and the first reinforcement-learning experiments with verifiable rewards. During the reported period, six continued pre-training campaigns were completed, culminating in a D500-Hybrid-v2 checkpoint trained on approximately 499 million tokens and achieving the lowest DEV loss measured in the program to date. The program also developed a scientific execution infrastructure integrating real numerical solvers, provenance, sandboxed execution, result verification, signed evidence packets, cost controls, and reproducible workflows. The report explicitly distinguishes between capabilities that have been demonstrated and those that remain under investigation. In particular, the scientific computing and verification infrastructure has been validated, while complete autonomous scientific tool use by the model has not yet been demonstrated. items.abstract: Abstract : This study aims to analyze the challenges of using Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) to understand the Qur’an and Hadith among undergraduate Islamic Education (PAI) students, their practices of information verification and academic integrity, and the application of Islamic ethics of seeking knowledge. This qualitative study employed a case study design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire comprising open-ended and closed-ended questions administered to 13 informants and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that Generative AI helps students understand learning materials and access information efficiently. However, its use presents risks, including inaccurate information, unclear sources, and reduced learning independence. Students reported verifying AI-generated information through Qur’anic commentaries, Hadith collections, scholarly literature, and consultations with lecturers or teachers, although verification practices varied. Ethical AI use requires honesty, trustworthiness, diligence, discipline, and responsibility to ensure that technology remains a learning aid rather than a substitute for independent thinking and engagement with authoritative Islamic sources.

items.title: Quantitative Study: The Effect of Digital Learning Media Interactivity on Children's Focus
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital learning media has intensified debate over which design characteristics most effectively support children's cognitive engagement. This study quantitatively examined the influence of digital learning media interactivity on children's learning focus, addressing a gap between the broader screen-time literature and the specific design features that shape sustained attention. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, involving 116 elementary school-aged children (6-12 years) who regularly used digital learning media, selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using a validated and reliable structured questionnaire measuring digital learning media interactivity (navigation, responsiveness, feedback, interactive engagement, and learner control) and children's learning focus (selective attention, sustained attention, attentional control, and task engagement) on a five-point Likert scale, then analyzed using descriptive statistics, classical assumption testing, and simple linear regression in IBM SPSS Statistics. Both interactivity (M = 2.95, SD = 0.68) and learning focus (M = 2.95, SD = 0.67) were rated at moderate levels. Regression analysis showed that interactivity significantly and positively predicted learning focus (β = 0.469, t = 5.732, p < .001), with a moderate correlation (r = .473) and the model explaining 22.4% of the variance (R² = .224; F(1,114) = 32.857, p < .001). These findings indicate that interactivity is a meaningful, modifiable design characteristic that enhances children's attentional engagement, offering empirical guidance for teachers, parents, and developers in prioritizing interactive features over passive content delivery to support classroom attention.

items.title: Re-focussing attention: stakeholder perspectives on the adoption and application of Driver Monitoring Systems in UK vehicles
items.abstract: Driver Monitoring Systems (DMS) are becoming increasingly integrated within modern vehicles, driven by advances in sensing technologies, artificial intelligence and evolving regulatory requirements. While previous research has largely focused on drivers’ perceptions and system performance, comparatively little attention has been given to the perspectives of the stakeholders who design, develop, regulate and implement these technologies. This study explored expert stakeholder views on the current role, challenges and future direction of DMS in the UK automotive sector. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven stakeholders representing vehicle manufacturers, applied research institutions, safety and regulatory experts, technology developers and testing organisations, and user experience (UX) design experts. Data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Six themes emerged: (1) DMS as a compliance-driven system; (2) misalignment with drivers’ mental models; (3) lack of personalisation; (4) intrusiveness and annoyance; (5) trust and acceptance; and (6) DMS as part of a broader socio-technical system. Stakeholders consistently viewed current DMS implementations as being driven primarily by regulatory compliance rather than user needs, with concerns that rigid thresholds, poorly calibrated alerts and limited transparency undermine driver trust and encourage system disengagement or misuse. Participants emphasised the importance of adaptive, context-aware and human-centred approaches to design that better accommodate individual differences while balancing privacy, usability and regulatory requirements. The findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of DMS depends not only on sensing performance but also on how systems interact with drivers within a wider socio-technical context. The study provides an expert stakeholder perspective that complements existing driver-focused research and identifies key priorities for future human factors research, including adaptive monitoring, improved human-machine interaction, regulatory evaluation and ethical governance. These findings offer practical insights for researchers, manufacturers and policymakers seeking to support the safe and acceptable deployment of next-generation driver monitoring technologies.

items.title: Real-time AI architectures for intraoperative surgical workflow: from temporal modeling and multi-modal fusion to efficient edge deployment
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into intraoperative surgical environments represents a transformative paradigm shift in modern surgery. Real-time surgical workflow recognition systems leverage sophisticated temporal modeling architectures, multi-modal data fusion strategies, and efficient edge deployment techniques to provide context-aware decision support during surgical procedures. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary advances in deep learning architectures for surgical video analysis, examining the evolution from recurrent neural networks to transformer-based models, the integration of heterogeneous data sources including video, kinematics, and sensor data, and the computational optimization strategies enabling deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. We critically analyze benchmark datasets, evaluate state-of-the-art performance metrics, and discuss the regulatory landscape governing AI-enabled surgical devices. The review identifies key challenges including context-dependent latency requirements—markedly stricter for robotic teleoperation control loops than for on-stream model inference, which need only keep pace with the ~25 fps surgical-video acquisition rate—together with robust generalization across surgical variations and standardized evaluation protocols. Emerging trends including foundation models for surgical video analysis and vision-language models for automated documentation are discussed, alongside future directions for clinical translation. items.title: Reality Image Model: A Unified Risk Modeling and Metrological Governance Framework for LLM Factual Hallucinations (RIM-H)
items.abstract: Reality Image Model: A Unified Risk Modeling and Metrological Governance Framework for LLM Factual Hallucinations (RIM-H) Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in complex knowledge reasoning and multi-task generation. However, "factual hallucination"—where models generate fluent yet factually unsupported or logically contradictory statements—remains the fundamental bottleneck impeding their deployment toward high reliability, safety alignment, and rigorous scientific applications. Existing governance paradigms (such as post-hoc fact-checking, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), or probabilistic calibration) largely remain fragmented, patch-oriented engineering heuristics, lacking a unified risk modeling framework grounded in information source epistemology and a rigorously falsifiable metrological system. Grounded in the forefront of independent research and building upon the author's foundational work in cognitive science and systems theory—Reality Image Theory (RIT)—this project systematically constructs the Reality Image Model for Hallucination Governance (RIM-H). Moving beyond conventional purely probabilistic perspectives, RIM-H reconceptualizes LLM factual errors as structural system risks within the full-chain evolution of "External Reality -> Accessible Information -> Reality Image -> Information Mediator -> Evidence Constraint." To address the critical metrological blind spot of "Atomic Claim Drift" and "Statistical Unit Drift" inherent in prior evaluation frameworks, this project has fully developed and statically frozen the Atomic Claim Parsing Protocol (ACP-v1.0.1). This establishes a fully auditable evidence chain spanning raw model responses to a four-layer isolated data architecture (Response -> Span -> Claim Instance -> Semantic Claim) paired with deterministic Log Loss recalculation. Achieving methodological saturation in theory and a rigorously isolated double-blind pilot execution framework in engineering, this project delivers a reproducible, scientifically rigorous governance paradigm for LLM factual hallucinations suitable for rigorous international peer review.

items.title: Reconceptualizing Teacher Professional Competence through Medical Biochemistry: A Biopsychological Framework Linking Biochemical Health, Cognitive Function, and Educational Effectiveness
items.abstract: Teacher professional competence has traditionally been theorized through pedagogical, cognitive, and motivational lenses, treating biological health as a peripheral concern rather than a core determinant of instructional capacity. This paper proposes a biopsychological reconceptualization of teacher competence that positions medical biochemistry-specifically micronutrient status, hormonal regulation, gut-brain signaling, sleep architecture, and stress-biomarker profiles-as a foundational layer underlying cognitive function and, by extension, classroom effectiveness. Drawing on peer-reviewed research published between 2020 and 2025 across educational psychology, endocrinology, nutritional science, and microbiome research, the paper synthesizes evidence linking biochemical dysregulation to impairments in working memory, attention, emotional regulation, and decision-making-the same cognitive-affective resources teachers draw on moment-to-moment in instructional practice. The paper proposes a biopsychological framework that models teaching competence as emerging from the interaction of biochemical health, cognitive-affective function, and pedagogical skill. The paper argues that teacher training, occupational wellness policy, and school-level health infrastructure should treat biochemical health as a professional-competence variable rather than a private lifestyle matter. It outlines practical implications for teacher education programs, occupational health policy, and future interdisciplinary research.

items.title: Regional Differences in Virtual Reality Aircraft Walk-Around Inspection Performance: Accuracy, Completion Time, and Spatial Ability
items.abstract: Aircraft walk-around inspection is a safety-critical task where human error plays a significant contributing role in maintenance-related incidents. Using immersive virtual reality (VR) for preparation has been suggested, but the effect of ergonomic complexity, defined as the postural and visual-search demands imposed by aircraft zone geometry, on inspection errors is unknown. This research applies a quasi-experimental within-subjects design (intact class, no randomization) to evaluate differences in novice trainee error rates between front-side and rear-side aircraft zone inspections applying an immersive VR aircraft inspection task (N = 40, aeronautical engineering students). The rear-side inspection scenario shows lower accuracy (p = 0.002, Cohen’s dz = 0.52) and longer completion time (p < 0.001, Cohen’s dz = 0.65) than the front-side scenario. Missed-defect rates and error-type frequencies are examined descriptively without an independent significance test of error-type composition. Spatial ability positively correlates with inspection accuracy (r = 0.62, p < 0.001). The findings indicate performance differences between the two simulated inspection scenarios, although the contributions of ergonomic complexity and other task characteristics could not be determined independently. Lastly, immersive VR may offer a viable preparatory training environment for identifying region-specific performance vulnerabilities and for identifying trainees who may benefit from additional preparation prior to on-aircraft hands-on practice.

items.title: RELEVANSI ONTOLOGI, EPISTEMOLOGI, DAN AKSIOLOGI DALAM PENDIDIKAN ISLAM DI ERA DIGITAL
items.abstract: The development of digital technology has brought significant changes to the processes of acquiring, developing, and disseminating knowledge in Islamic education. Easy access to information and the use of artificial intelligence have created opportunities for learning innovation while also raising concerns regarding the nature of education, the validity of knowledge, and the cultivation of students’ values and moral character. These developments highlight the need to re-examine the relevance of the philosophical foundations of Islamic education in the face of digital transformation. This study aims to analyze the relevance of ontology, epistemology, and axiology in Islamic education in the digital era. It employs a qualitative approach using library research. Data were collected through the identification and documentation of relevant books, scholarly journal articles, and academic publications, and were analyzed using a descriptive-analytical technique involving thematic categorization and conceptual synthesis. The findings indicate that ontology plays a role in affirming the nature of human beings as subjects of education who possess intellectual, spiritual, and moral dimensions. Epistemology provides a foundation for developing critical thinking skills, verifying information, and integrating revelation, reason, and experience in the acquisition of knowledge. Meanwhile, axiology guides the use of technology in accordance with Islamic values, digital ethics, responsibility, and moral character development. These three dimensions are interrelated in shaping an Islamic education system that adapts to technological advancements without losing sight of its values and educational objectives. This study concludes that the integration of ontology, epistemology, and axiology is essential to realizing an Islamic education system that is critical, humanistic, and firmly grounded in Islamic values in the digital era.
