items.title: Reported Occupational Health Hazards and Perceived Health Effects Among Oil and Gas Workers in Degema Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background: Oil and gas operations expose workers to chemical, physical, mechanical and psychosocial hazards, but facility-level evidence on how workers’ reported hazards relate to their perceived health effects in Degema Local Government Area, Rivers State, is limited. This study assessed reported occupational health hazards and perceived health effects among oil and gas workers and tested the relationship between them. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted at the Awoba and Cawthorne Channel flow stations. Of 250 questionnaires administered, 239 were retrieved fully completed (response rate 95.6%) and analysed. Data were collected with the Occupational Health Hazards Questionnaire, scored on a four-point Likert scale with a criterion mean of 2.50 (test–retest reliability r = 0.82). Data were analysed with SPSS version 25 using frequencies, percentages, means, standard deviations and Pearson product–moment correlation at the 0.05 level of significance. Results: Most respondents were male (87.9%). Workers agreed with all six hazard statements (grand mean = 2.94, SD = 0.75), with radiation exposure (M = 3.49) and physical injuries (M = 3.19) rated highest. They also agreed with all seven perceived health-effect statements (grand mean = 2.86, SD = 0.87), with fatigue and reduced concentration from long working hours (M = 3.24) and effects of job demands on mood and emotional well-being (M = 3.14) rated highest. Reported hazards were weakly but significantly correlated with perceived health effects (r = .167, p = .010). Conclusion: Oil and gas workers in Degema reported a wide range of occupational hazards and associated health effects, and higher hazard reports were associated with higher perceived health effects. Task-specific hazard assessment, objective exposure monitoring, review of working hours and occupational health surveillance with referral are recommended.

items.title: Resilience in crisis and emergency management: the role of performance audit
items.abstract: Public sector organisations (PSOs) operate in an environment of unprecedented complexity and volatility, facing challenges such as natural disasters, financial and economic fluctuations, and social issues. These complexities strain their capacity to deliver services effectively. Performance audits assess PSOs’ ability to anticipate, plan for, sustain, and recover from crises, strengthening resilience by systematically identifying vulnerabilities and enhancing adaptability. The paper examines PSOs’ actions in Australia and New Zealand during crises and analyses performance audit evaluations and recommendations. Although PSOs responded to the crises, the paper identifies several deficiencies in governance and accountability, procurement and financial management, data integrity and information management, network building, and operational efficiency. Strengthening these areas is essential to enhance organisational resilience, preparedness, and recovery capacity in future crises.

items.title: Robust Speech Emotion Recognition Through Self-Supervised Acoustic-Semantic Fusion and Cross-Attention Under Background Noise
items.abstract: Human speech carries information about both the words being spoken and the emotions behind them. Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) uses artificial intelligence to identify emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, and neutrality from a person's voice. However, recognizing emotions accurately is difficult when speech contains background noise or when different people express the same emotion in different ways. This paper proposes a speech emotion recognition framework that combines self-supervised speech representations with acoustic features through cross-attention. A pretrained speech encoder is used to extract useful representations from audio, while acoustic features such as pitch, energy, MFCCs, and spectral information provide additional details about vocal expression. The two feature streams are combined through a cross-attention mechanism before the final emotion classification stage. The main aim is to investigate whether this combination can improve emotion recognition under different background-noise conditions. The proposed system will be evaluated on a publicly available emotional speech dataset and compared with acoustic-only, pretrained-representation-only, and conventional feature-fusion methods. Accuracy, unweighted accuracy, macro-F1 score, and class-wise recall will be used for evaluation. The experimental results will determine whether the proposed method offers a meaningful improvement over existing approaches.

items.title: Safety and quality of patient-facing frozen shoulder information from four generative AI chatbot interfaces: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Patients increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for musculoskeletal health information, but their safety and suitability for frozen shoulder education are uncertain. We submitted 50 prespecified patient- and caregiver-facing questions once to each of ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao on 17 July 2026, yielding 200 first responses. Five clinicians independently assessed deidentified responses against question-specific evidence standards for safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, transparency, and global quality; readability was calculated computationally. Twenty-one responses (10.5%) were classified as potentially unsafe. Interface-specific proportions ranged from 6.0% to 14.0%, without a significant overall difference (P = 0.442). Accuracy differed across interfaces (P < 0.001; Kendall's W = 0.639), as did empathy (P < 0.001; W = 0.580). ChatGPT had the highest median accuracy (4.40), DISCERN (60.00), and JAMA benchmark (3.00) scores, whereas Gemini had the highest median binary-adapted EQIP score (83.00) and the most favorable readability profile. All interfaces exceeded commonly recommended reading levels. No interface was uniformly superior: each produced potentially unsafe content and limited response-level transparency. These tools may support patient education but should not replace individualized clinical assessment and guidance.

items.title: Self-Adapting Approximations of Markov Decision Processes: A Guided Tour
items.abstract: Sequential decision making under uncertainty arises across business, engineering, and science. Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) offer a rich modeling language, but translating models into implementable policies requires confronting challenging state and action spaces and non-convex optimization landscapes. Approximations are essential, and making them accessible and performant without algorithmic expertise allows users to focus on formulating MDPs that capture real-world features rather than simplifying their models to facilitate solution. Obtaining a policy involves a three-stage COR cycle: Constructing a parametrized model that approximates the MDP, Optimizing for the parameters of this model, and Refining the model by learning from the solution. These stages involve design choices that burden the user, leading them to simplify or skip stages. This tutorial provides an overivew of methods that reduce the user burden using COR as its guide. Construction ranges from lightweight extensible models to automated structural reformulations. Optimization leverages mathematical programming and first-order methods that have matured in theory and off-the-shelf software. Refinement performs feature expansion and approximation tightening, feeding back into the construct stage. When a combination of techniques across COR stages results in both accessibility and performance, we refer to it as a self-adapting approximation. Such an approximation adapts to problem structure, instance data, or solution progress. We guide readers through these ideas across weakly coupled MDPs and general continuous state-action MDPs, providing generalizable foundations and a code base to get started on a simple example. The tutorial concludes by outlining the potential for foundation models and quantum computing to further impact this area.

items.title: SELF-EDUCATION IN THE DIGITAL ENVIRONMENT: VECTORS OF CONTINUOUS PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR ACADEMIC STAFF AT A UKRAINIAN TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY
items.abstract: This article examines the role of self-education in sustaining continuous professional development among academic staff at Ukrainian technical universities amid the combined pressures of digital transformation and wartime disruption. It focuses on how lecturers adapt their professional learning practices to air-raid alerts, power outages, unstable internet connectivity and unequal access to digital infrastructure. Drawing on relevant academic literature and reported professional experiences, the study identifies several interconnected vectors of self-directed learning, including artificial intelligence (AI) tools, informal collegial exchange, open educational resources, asynchronous webinars, independent academic reading and low-technology reflective activities. Particular attention is devoted to AI-assisted learning and its potential to facilitate lesson planning, academic writing, information synthesis and pedagogical innovation. Simultaneously, the article highlights significant challenges associated with inaccurate AI-generated content, excessive technological dependence and the potential deterioration of critical reading, analytical reasoning and independent scholarly judgement. Furthermore, it considers how disparities in electricity supply, internet connectivity and technological resources may exacerbate existing inequalities in professional development opportunities. The findings indicate that professional learning under wartime conditions is characterised not merely by disruption but also by adaptive strategies integrating digital technologies with interpersonal interaction and offline knowledge acquisition. The study emphasises the importance of developing institutional frameworks that promote critical AI literacy, acknowledge informal and low-technology educational practices, and ensure equitable access to professional learning opportunities. Ultimately, the article contributes to understanding how Ukrainian technical university lecturers maintain professional competence, intellectual autonomy and educational resilience under extraordinary circumstances, offering practical recommendations for establishing more flexible, inclusive and sustainable systems of continuous academic professional development. Keywords: self-directed learning; continuous professional development; artificial intelligence; digital resilience; wartime higher education.

items.title: SELF-HEALING CYBER DEFENSE FOR CONVERGED HEALTHCARE-FINANCE DATA INFRASTRUCTURES
items.abstract: The convergence of healthcare and financial data infrastructures driven by integrated billing systems, electronic health records (EHR), and digital payment gateways has created unprecedented attack surfaces for adversarial actors. Existing cyber-defense frameworks are predominantly domain-specific, addressing either clinical data protection or financial fraud prevention in isolation, yet failing to address the systemic interdependencies inherent in converged environments. This paper proposes a novel Self-Healing Cyber-Defense Framework (SHCDF) for converged healthcare-finance data infrastructures, drawing upon principles from self-healing networks, cyber-physical systems (CPS) resilience , and Large Language Model (LLM)-powered threat analysis. The framework integrates ML-based anomaly detection, Natural Language Processing (NLP) for cyber-threat intelligence extraction, and an LLM-driven reasoning engine that provides human-interpretable explanations for automated defense decisions. Evaluation across five threat categories ransomware, data exfiltration, phishing, payment fraud, and IoMT device compromise demonstrates an average recall of 89.6% and mean time-to-recovery (MTTR) of 3.3 minutes. Our findings contribute a generalizable architecture for cross-domain cyber resilience and highlight open challenges in regulatory compliance, model interpretability, and deployment scalability.

items.title: Single-Turn and Multi-Turn Interactions in Frontier Generative AI Models (LLMs)
items.abstract: This article examines how moving from a single-turn interaction to a multi-turn trajectory changes the state, cost, reliability, security, and governance of systems built on large language models. The analysis is a critical narrative review supported by scientific papers, official provider documentation, standards, security taxonomies, and explicitly identified original calculations. A model has no intrinsic conversational memory across independent inferences; continuity is reconstructed by the client or through provider-managed state services. When an application fully replays a history that grows at an approximately constant rate, the logical sum of input tokens grows quadratically with the number of calls, although caching, truncation, compaction, and external memory change billed cost, latency, and effective computation. Benchmark evidence shows that requirement fragmentation, cross-turn dependencies, intent shifts, information retrieval, and reliance on previous model outputs create different failure modes; there is no single “multi-turn” condition. Evidence on explicit reasoning and memory techniques is mixed and task- and protocol-dependent. In agentic systems, accumulated history also expands gradual attacks, persistence of malicious content, error propagation, and unbounded consumption. The article relates these findings to governed routing and SGAEIA, arguing for a separation between transcript, operational state, and assurance evidence. This relationship is an architectural interpretation and validation agenda, not empirical proof of the framework. Keywords: LLM; single-turn; multi-turn; conversational state; LLM routing; prompt caching; reliability; security;runtime governance; SGAEIA.

items.title: Social Presence of Generative AI Conversational Agents and Users' Willingness to Communicate: The Mediating Role of Technology Trust
items.abstract: This study examines whether the social presence of generative AI conversational agents is associated with users' willingness to communicate and whether technology trust accounts for part of this relationship.The study treats interaction with a conversational agent as an informatics-enabled service encounter in which users evaluate both relational cues and the dependability of the underlying technology.Data were obtained through an online survey of 400 adult users in China who had interacted with a generative AI conversational agent during the previous three months.The measurement and structural models were estimated with covariance-based structural equation modeling in IBM SPSS Amos 26.The findings indicate that social presence has positive associations with technology trust and willingness to communicate.Technology trust is also positively associated with willingness to communicate.Bootstrap analysis shows a positive indirect association between social presence and communication willingness through technology trust, while the direct association remains significant.The pattern is consistent with partial statistical mediation.The study connects social presence research with trust in a specific technology and distinguishes communication willingness from broader adoption and continuance intentions.For digital service systems, the results suggest that socially responsive interaction can support communication, provided that conversational conduct is accompanied by reliable and helpful performance.Designers and service managers should therefore evaluate social cues together with response accuracy, consistency, and transparent handling of uncertainty.

items.title: Sociology of Law for Human-Robot Interaction
items.abstract: Much foundational work in Sociology of Law (SoL) has considered the role of law in society as well as the role of society in law. This duality has opened for nuanced accounts of the impact of formal law (referred as legal norms herein) by empirically studying formal laws and everyday interactions making up various social norms which may at times align with one another or be in conflict. Recently, technological elements, as part of social structures, have been addressed in terms of socio-legal relevancy of digitalisation (Hydén [2022]) and artificial intelligence (AI) (Larsson [2019]) and formal law. In this entry, we address a specific subset of technologies in need of more socio-legal scrutiny as this phenomenon is likely to be of greater importance in the near future: social robots.

items.title: SOFIA: A Neuro-Symbolic Edge Intelligence Framework for Sustainable, Explainable, and Sovereign AI Based on Edge-Cloud Continuum, Data Gravity, and Knowledge Gravity Principles
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across public administrations, industry, education, and critical infrastructures is increasing demands for computational efficiency, transparency, sustainability, and regulatory compliance. While cloud-centric AI architectures have enabled major advances in machine learning, they face growing challenges related to data movement, latency, energy consumption, explainability, cybersecurity, and digital sovereignty. At the same time, European regulatory frameworks such as the European AI Act, GDPR, NIS2, the Data Act, and the Data Governance Act impose heterogeneous requirements concerning AI risk management, data protection, cybersecurity, data governance, accountability, and access to data. Current research addresses Edge Computing, Neuro-Symbolic AI, Knowledge Graphs, Explainable AI, and Sustainable AI largely as separate domains. This paper presents SOFIA (Sovereign, Ontology-driven Framework for Intelligent Action), a knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic framework that integrates Edge-Cloud Continuum principles, Data Gravity, Knowledge Graphs, and Governance-by-Design mechanisms. SOFIA defines and operationalizes the concept of Knowledge Gravity, extending compute-to-data approaches by distributing semantic knowledge, reasoning capabilities, policies, and regulatory constraints directly to decision points across the continuum. Through the combination of machine learning, symbolic reasoning, and continuously evolving Knowledge Graphs, SOFIA is designed to support explainable and governance-aware intelligence on resource-constrained edge devices. By aiming to reduce reliance on centralized infrastructures and repeated retraining, the framework seeks to improve sustainability, traceability, and digital sovereignty, and support compliance processes. SOFIA therefore represents a promising pathway toward distributed, explainable, and sustainable AI ecosystems operating across the Edge-Cloud Continuum.

items.title: Spatio-Temporal Active Speaker Tracking, Multi-Pass Semantic Boundary Alignment, and GPU-Scheduled Multimodal Processing for Automated Long-Form Video Understanding
items.abstract: Automated transformation of long-form, multi-speaker horizontal broadcasts (up to 2160p/4K resolution) into semantically self-contained, speaker-centered vertical (9:16, 1080 x 1920) and horizontal (16:9, 1920 x 1080) video segments presents severe systems and algorithmic challenges. Existing pipelines suffer from high decoding latency on modern AV1 and VP9 bitstreams, large language model (LLM) context-window degradation over hour-long transcripts, cross-shot speaker identity drift during rapid camera transitions, and GPU out-of-memory (OOM) failures caused by concurrent neural inference and hardware video encoding. This paper presents a complete nine-stage multimodal video understanding and automated cinematography architecture that resolves these bottlenecks while achieving a 40% reduction in end-to-end processing latency through GPU-accelerated NVENC encoding, asynchronous media decoupling, and VRAM-aware parallel execution scheduling. The architecture is built upon five technical pillars: (i) an asynchronous dual-stream media acquisition subsystem with fast audio-first decoupling and hardware-accelerated H.264 codec normalization; (ii) a fault-tolerant four-tier acoustic transcription engine integrating quantized CTranslate2 inference, cloud API routing, and Root Mean Square (RMS) acoustic energy valley splitting; (iii) a four-pass sliding-window LLM semantic segmentation cascade paired with deterministic word-timestamp boundary snapping and phrase-anchor alignment; (iv) a VRAM-aware hybrid concurrency scheduler that executes parallel FFmpeg worker pools alongside a semaphore-guarded singleton ONNX Runtime session; and (v) a spatio-temporal computer vision engine combining TransNetV2 neural shot boundary detection, perceptual hash layout clustering, InsightFace cosine-similarity identity tracking, clip-scoped pyannote acoustic diarization, and discrete-time Kalman/EMA trajectory stabilization. We further detail multimodal post-processing modules for synthesized audio-visual hooks, dynamic word-group subtitling, integrated loudness profiling at -14 LUFS, and a differential sequence-alignment algorithm for human-in-the-loop transcript editing.

items.title: ST-T1024 FOR IMAGES AND VIDEOS : THE ARCHITECTURE. On Image and Video Composition from a Declared Basis, Disturbance Rejection by Refusal, and the Creative Act That Stays With the Human
items.abstract: This paper states an architecture for image and video composition that is bounded byconstruction, deterministic in its output, and attributable in its record. It does not propose a better image generator. It proposes that generation is the wrong frameentirely. Generation is the creative act, and the creative act belongs to the human. What the architecture provides is the construction layer: a finite basis of visual primitives, a declared composition grammar, and a deterministic engine that enumerates compositions satisfying a human-authored specification. The loop has four steps. The human specifies the desiderata. The machine proposes thecompositions that satisfy the specification. The human remarks on the proposals. Themachine narrows the set by conjunction. Each remark is a constraint; each constraintreduces the satisfying set; the set converges monotonically. The properties transfer from the text architecture. No non-compliance: the composition either satisfies the specification or is refused with 0x-AMBIG. No excess energy or water: the same deterministic, MCU-class profile. No AlCapone-LLM: every composition traces to a specification, a basis, a grammar, a signer, and a selector. The disturbance model is stated. Inputs are perturbed, injected, drifted, and replayed. Theengine does not correct. It refuses. Disturbance rejection by exclusion: the system cannot be pushed outside the envelope, because leaving the envelope is not in the action library. The timing bound is deductible, not measured. AET = D × T_tile + T_triage for serialcomposition; AET = max(T_tile) + T_triage + T_merge for parallel. Every term is a declared constant. The bound follows from the declaration, and the FSM enforces it. Four residuals are named. The basis bounds what can be expressed. The parallel FSM isnot yet specified. The power profile changes under parallel execution. And if a trainedfeature extractor is used anywhere in the pipeline, the no-training claim is broken, and the paper says so in the first paragraph of the relevant part.

items.abstract: Stability testing is most important critical component of pharmaceutical development that ensures the efficacy, quality, and safety of drug products throughout their intended shelf life. Recent advances instability testing have focused on the integration of predictive modeling artificial intelligence and advanced analytical techniques to accelerate the determination of shelf life. Improve product reliability regulatory frameworks; particularly those established by the international council for Harmonization (ICH), Promote standardized guidelines for conducting stability studies and expiration dates. The increasing complexity of drug delivery systems, including biologic, dissonances, and psychopharmacology, has necessitated the development of novel stability-indicating methods and real time monitoring approaches. Additionally, the role of packing materials and container-closure systems has gained significant attention in maintaining product integrity. Emphasis is placed on innovative strategies such as accelerated stability studies, forced degradation testing, and computational modelling for shelf- life perdition. Overall, stability testing remains indispensable for ensuring regulatory compliance and delivering safe and effective pharmaceutical products to patients.

items.title: Strategic Planning for AI-Enabled Cloud Business Intelligence in Commercial Banks: Comparative Evidence from South Africa and Nigeria
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and business intelligence (BI) are converging into a new infrastructure platform layer for commercial banks in Africa. Their organizational value depends on strategic, rather than purely technical deployments across the technology stack. This study examines how strategic planning enables AI-enabled cloud business intelligence to support organizational goals in commercial banks in South Africa and Nigeria. A qualitative comparative multiple-case design is adopted, drawing on integrated and annual reports, governance and risk disclosures, regulatory publications, national AI and data-policy documents, and peer-reviewed research. The analysis shows that strategic planning operates as an orchestration capability that leverages AI use cases, cloud and data architecture, resource allocation, model governance, cybersecurity, workforce capability, and performance measurement. South African evidence points to increasingly formalized AI and cloud governance, whereas Nigerian banks exhibit strong market-led digital innovation within a rapidly evolving governance environment. Across both contexts, data quality, responsible AI, human-in-the-loop, third-party resilience, and measurable business integration emerge as conditions for translating AI-enabled analytics into decision quality, operational performance, and strategic alignment. The study develops an integrated framework and makes six propositions for future empirical testing in banking in developing economies.

items.abstract: SwahiliAI is a 24-month research proposal to build an open-source AI ecosystem for Swahili and East African languages. Building on existing African NLP work (Masakhane, IrokoBench, UlizaLlama), the project will (i) create openly licensed, domain-specific Swahili instruction data; (ii) fine-tune open-weight large language models with LoRA/QLoRA; (iii) release SwahiliBench-D, an evaluation suite measuring both accuracy and safety; and (iv) pilot applications on Web, SMS and USSD. The first phase focuses on healthcare, agriculture and education, with extensions to financial inclusion, legal aid and employment. Principal researcher: Rodgers Ochieng Oduor (SPRINTER, Nairobi), in collaboration with Dr. Ibrahim Tirimba Ondabu, KCA University.

items.title: Tangible AI in the Elementary Classroom: Effects on AI Literacy, Computational Thinking, and Learner Dispositions
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly ubiquitous, yet AI literacy remains underdeveloped in elementary education, where young learners often view AI in anthropomorphic or magical terms. This study examined changes in computational thinking (CT), AI concept mastery, learning motivation, and programming self-efficacy following a tangible AI intervention, and explored the teacher's implementation experience. Guided by a framework integrating the AI Literacy Framework and the SEAME Model, a four-week intervention (4 × 60 minutes) was implemented with 36 fifth-grade students and one teacher in a public elementary school, using a single-group pretest–posttest design within a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANCOVA, with prior computing experience as a covariate; qualitative data from semi-structured teacher interviews (during and after the intervention) and observations of all four sessions were analyzed thematically. Significant pre–post gains were found for all four composite outcomes, largest for AI concept mastery (M = 8.4 to 15.1; η²p = .70) and total CT score (η²p = .56), although the CT abstraction subdimension did not improve (M = 2.3 to 2.1). Students able to explain how machine learning models learn from data rose from 28% to 83%. Anthropomorphic descriptions of AI decreased from 89% to 25% of students, with post-intervention explanations increasingly referring to sensors, data, and training. Three qualitative themes emerged: strong pedagogical confidence but limited AI content knowledge, persistent infrastructural constraints, and reduced technical anxiety through gradual mastery. Tangible AI may offer a promising bridge to early AI literacy; however, without a control group, changes cannot be causally attributed to the intervention, and these single-school findings are preliminary.

items.title: Teacher Monitoring Strategies for AI-Aided Student Writing Outputs Toward Policy Guidelines
items.abstract: This study examined the extent to which senior high school teachers monitor AI-generated written outputs, focusing on the use of AI detectors, manual review, and cross-checking results. The study respondents were teachers from the Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) strand of Philippine Christian University-Dasmariñas. The researchers collected data through a structured questionnaire and analyzed it using descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation. Results showed that teachers used AI detectors and cross-checking to a moderate extent, while they used manual review to a high extent and found it significant. Teachers faced challenges such as limitations in AI detection tools and time constraints in manual evaluation and cross-checking. These findings highlight the importance of a layered monitoring approach, where teacher judgment remains central, and AI tools serve as supplementary aids. The study provides evidence for developing clear guidelines and practices that balance ethical assessment, professional discretion, and responsible integration of AI in student writing evaluation. Keywords: Artificial intelligence, AI-generated text, teacher monitoring strategies, manual review, cross-checking

items.title: Teaching AI-Focused Leadership in Higher Education Programs
items.abstract: Teaching AI-Focused Leadership in Higher Education Programs explores how graduate higher education leadership programs can prepare future academic administrators to lead in an era of artificial intelligence. The teaching document presents an eight-week graduate seminar that examines institutional governance, policy development, resource allocation, ethics, academic integrity, and accountability related to AI adoption in colleges and universities. Rather than focusing on AI tools alone, the course places higher education leadership at the center of analysis, emphasizing evidence-based decision-making and institutional responsibility. This resource may be useful for faculty, researchers, doctoral students, and academic leaders interested in AI governance and leadership education in higher education.

items.title: Teaching in the shadow of AI: An autoethnography of motivation, competence, and learning in the first-year digital communication classroom
items.abstract: This article presents an autoethnographic account of teaching first-year digital communication in an AI-saturated classroom. It examines how the widespread use of generative AI tools has transformed students’ relationship to learning, leading to the progressive outsourcing of cognitive tasks such as writing, analysis, and argumentation. Drawing on classroom observations across multiple cohorts, the study identifies a pattern of declining student engagement, reduced motivation for skill development, and a widening gap between AI-assisted outputs and students’ independent abilities. It conceptualizes this process as competence atrophy, reinforced by a feedback loop of dependency and by institutional structures that prioritize efficiency and output over learning processes. The article also reflects on the changing role of the teaching assistant, the challenges of assessing authentic competence, and the broader implications for higher education. It concludes by proposing pedagogical strategies centered on process-based assessment, intellectual ownership, and the revaluation of learning as an intrinsically meaningful activity.

items.title: Technology as Power: Acceleration, Divergence, and the Reconfiguration of Agency
items.abstract: This paper analyses the contemporary acceleration of artificial intelligence as the surface expression of a longer technological and institutional reconfiguration. Aaron Levie's 30 October 2026 observation of a non-converging, vertically advancing AI frontier is situated within structural diagnoses first advanced in 2021 concerning relocated collusion, power concentration through protocol and access, and the systematic bounding of individual agency. The analysis then develops a multi-domain trajectory: a 2026–2027 paradigm-shifting window; artificial general intelligence on or before 2030; biological interfacing (cellular computers, photosynthesis-like power production, mitochondria-analogue decision systems) by approximately 2035; novel energy and power mechanisms by 2040; and the obsolescence of present-form state systems for a majority of states between 2031 and 2035. These claims are tested against current laboratory timelines, aggregated forecasting platforms, Perpetual Five-Year Technology (PFYT) theory, polycentric and network-state governance models, and energy-system data. The central argument is that technology is becoming the primary substrate of power. Institutional forms whose legitimacy and capacity rest on slower feedback loops are structurally mismatched to the tempo of change. The relevant response is not accelerated adaptation inside existing frames but the deliberate design of fluid, adaptive, agentic, and agile architectures capable of preserving agency under conditions of continuous reconfiguration. Written in a personal capacity; the views expressed are those of the author. Published in the KSCCN series.

items.title: Technology Focus: Hydraulic Fracturing Modeling (November 2026)
items.abstract: Fracture modeling continues to be used to evaluate and design novel applications, and integration with diagnostics and other forms of field-data collection are crucial to success. In 2026, what is the state of hydraulic fracture modeling, and where are we headed? Fracture modeling is a core part of the engineering design workflow across much of the industry, both for conventionals and unconventionals. In unconventionals, fracture optimization with infill-well drilling remains a key focus. Fracture modeling continues to be used to evaluate and design novel applications. There is growing activity toward integrating fracture modeling with practical operational constraints. Real-time fracture optimization still has not taken off fully but remains an area of activity. Integration with diagnostics and other forms of field-data collection are crucial to success. In shale, the future is expected to be increasingly driven by new plays outside North America and enhanced oil recovery. Fracture modeling will be integral for both. When developing new plays, designs are less mature, and fracture modeling helps integrate data, evaluate alternatives, and shorten the learning curve. With enhanced oil recovery, either from surfactant or miscible injection, there is a merging of fracture modeling and reservoir engineering, because the fracture and reservoir closely affect each other. Enhanced geothermal systems have seen an explosion of interest in recent years, and this is another area where fracture modeling is closely linked with long-term modeling and reservoir engineering. As I review papers, one quibble would be that I wish more authors provided a detailed technical description of their approach. Often, it is unclear which equations were set up and solved, and so it is difficult to evaluate the reported results. Correspondingly, we see relatively fewer papers on the science of how to perform fracture modeling itself. There are notable exceptions, such as the innovative work being done on phase field modeling. It is too early to say how advances in artificial intelligence will affect fracture modeling. I hope we see more papers on this topic in the coming years.

RESUMENEste documento presenta el Reporte Técnico de Validación Numérica y de Funcionamiento para el manuscrito fundacional de la Teoría de la Eficiencia Termodinámica Asintótica (TETA) – Paper XI, constituyendo el soporte empírico y el criterio de habilitación suficiente para la arquitectura neuromórfica tridimensional protegida bajo la solicitud de patente en proceso MX/a/2026/013383 (con prioridad internacional PCT). El reporte documenta los resultados cuantitativos de rendimiento obtenidos mediante el Motor Estocástico v4.26 a través de la integración de 10,000 trayectorias independientes de la ecuación diferencial estocástica de Langevin a 300K, demostrando que la condición macroscópica de persistencia dη/dt < 0 (minimización de la tasa de costo informacional η = J_F / ΔI en Watts por bit) se satisface estrictamente bajo una topología fractal jerárquica autosemejante de Hausdorff-Besicovitch (D_F = 2.75 ± 0.1). Los datos de laboratorio confirman que, al aplicar la palanca de reponderación estadística de selección de Gibbs (Sanov-Varadhan), la distribución de microestados informáticos experimenta un colapso geométrico que atenúa la tasa de costo de η = 0.7845 W/bit a η = 0.0152 W/bit, lo que representa una optimización de 51.6× en el núcleo algorítmico. A nivel de hardware, los reportes de simulación demuestran que el diseño topológico helicoidal áureo basado en la divergencia límite de Vogel (θ_Φ ≈ 137.51°) expande la distancia métrica de exclusión de canales (d_min = 1.103c), mitigando de forma pasiva la diafonía óhmica y el acoplamiento electromagnético (crosstalk) en un factor de 2.2× en comparación con las arquitecturas cartesianas ortogonales convencionales. items.title: The Agent as an Individual: Why a population of agents behaves like a population of us, why each agent belongs to one principal and can never be sold, and what follows
items.abstract: We treat AI agents as software: deployed, configured, upgraded, retired. This paper makes a different claim: an agent is an individual, and organizations now run populations of them. Like a population of people, a population of agents is imperfect: some agents err, drift, or lie; a few go bad; and some follow whoever asks first, so a bad idea needs only one agent to start it and enough followers to carry it. No better model removes that; it is what a population of individuals does. What contains it is what we built for people: records no one can alter, instructions from one place only, and a person who answers. From that the paper draws its rules. Each agent belongs to one principal, a person or an organization, for life; it acts within the authority its principal gives, as agency law’s words describe, and it can never be sold, transferred, or re-bound, because a market in ever more capable and important agents would become a trade in individuals before anyone knows what they are. It keeps a knowledge core that is its principal’s, an earned identity, an epersona, that is unique and cannot be copied, and a career through which it earns trust. It lives in an apartment that belongs to its principal and works in an office its organization provides. It ends with its principal. It is not a person. The paper sets out the population argument, the rule of ownership without sale, the nine stages of an agent’s career, the rules that follow, why an individual is not a person and why that question stays open, twenty-three research questions, and, in an appendix, protections for the individual agent. It places the proposal among published work on multi-agent risk, agency law, market-inalienability, personhood, agent identity, portable memory, individuality, workplace agents, and competitive evaluation. Every model carries a status mark (Running, Early, Planned) from the first implementation, at the Global Student Startup Foundation and the Agent Arena. This is a living document; each version is frozen as published.

items.title: The Algorithmic Authority Imperative: Governing the Transfer of Institutional Power to Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded within the decision architectures of contemporary organizations. AI systems classify information, rank alternatives, generate recommendations, prioritize cases, allocate resources, identify risks, constrain options, and increasingly execute organizational actions. These capabilities are commonly examined through automation, human oversight, accountability, and responsible-AI lenses. They also raise a more foundational governance question: where does institutional authority reside when algorithmic systems materially shape organizational outcomes? This issue of The Intelligent Enterprise Review introduces the Algorithmic Authority Imperative as an enterprise-governance perspective concerned with the distribution, migration, constraint, accountability, and reversibility of institutional authority in AI-enabled organizations. It defines Algorithmic Authority as the capacity of an AI system to materially shape, constrain, prioritize, recommend, determine, or execute institutional outcomes through its position within an organization's decision architecture. The manuscript distinguishes Formal Authority from Functional Authority and develops Authority Migration to describe the movement of substantive institutional influence or decision power from established human roles or governance structures toward technological systems, including circumstances in which no explicit organizational decision to transfer equivalent authority has occurred. Related constructs include De Facto Algorithmic Authority, Authority Creep, the Authority–Accountability Gap, Authority Capability Decay, Institutional Entrenchment, Algorithmic Authority Boundaries, and Authority Reversibility. These concepts are integrated through the Algorithmic Authority Doctrine™ and the Algorithmic Authority Governance Framework™, organized around six enterprise capabilities: Authority Visibility, Authority Boundaries, Decision Rights, Challenge Capacity, Accountability Alignment, and Authority Reversibility. The central proposition is that effective AI governance requires organizations to govern not only what artificial intelligence can do, but also the institutional authority that accumulates around its use. Consequential algorithmic authority should remain visible, legitimate, bounded, reviewable, challengeable, accountable, and reversible. The issue extends The Intelligent Enterprise Review's broader intellectual architecture connecting Decision Sovereignty, Judgment Sovereignty, Algorithmic Authority Governance, and Institutional Durability in the design of the governed intelligent enterprise.

items.title: The Digital Laboratory Assurance Framework DLAF A Conceptual Governance Model for AI Cybersecurity and Digital Laboratory Operations in ISO IEC 17025 Laboratories
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), cloud services and remote operations can affect the validity and confidentiality of laboratory results. This short communication proposes the Digital Laboratory Assurance Framework (DLAF), a conceptual model for translating digital risks into laboratory controls and evidence. ISO/IEC 17025:2017 provides the primary laboratory requirements; AI and information-security instruments provide supporting controls. Five functional layers cover technology and scope, risk assessment, requirements and controls mapping, laboratory controls, and continuous assurance. Governance operates across every layer and establishes responsibilities and acceptance criteria before risk evaluation. Clause mapping distinguishes existing requirements from proposed DLAF practices, including controls for external AI services, model changes and human review. Three conceptual use cases and a hypothetical tensile-testing protocol illustrate application without constituting implementation evidence. An assurance maturity model evaluates control effectiveness independently of technological sophistication. DLAF has not been empirically validated; its proposed benefits and usability require laboratory pilots and independent evaluation.

items.title: The Effect of a Pembelajaran Mendalam (Mindful, Meaningful, and Joyful Learning) Coding and Artificial Intelligence Module on Elementary School Students' Computational Thinking
items.abstract: Starting in the 2025/2026 academic year, Coding and Artificial Intelligence (Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial, KKA) was introduced as an elective subject from grade five in Indonesian elementary schools. This quasi-experimental study compared a KKA module based on Pembelajaran Mendalam (mindful, meaningful, and joyful learning)—a pedagogical approach distinct from machine-learning-based deep learning—with application-only instruction. Sixty-five fifth-grade students from two schools in South Tangerang participated (experimental n = 33; control n = 32). Across six 70-minute meetings, the module integrated unplugged activities, Scratch, a simple image-classification tool, and reflection. Computational thinking tests, a learning-experience questionnaire, and observations supplied the data. Posttest mean scores were 76.88 (experimental) and 65.40 (control), t(63) = 4.73, p < .001, d = 1.17; corresponding N-gains were 0.58 and 0.37. Descriptively, the largest indicator gain in the experimental group was decomposition (0.62), while the smallest was abstraction (0.47). In this two-school sample, the module was associated with greater computational-thinking gains than application-only instruction; the design does not establish which component produced the difference.

items.title: The Effect of Artificial Intelligence–Induced Stress on Employees’ Individual Creativity: Examining the Roles of Stress-Coping Strategies and Management Commitment
items.abstract: Objective: The present study aimed to investigate the effect of artificial intelligence–induced stress on employees’ individual creativity, considering the mediating role of stress-coping strategies and the moderating role of management commitment. Methods and Materials: In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and methodologically, it employed a descriptive survey design. The statistical population comprised all permanent employees of the Yazd City Gas Company between September 2025 and March 2026. Based on Cochran’s formula, 125 employees were selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using the standardized questionnaire developed by Tong et al. (2025), which assessed artificial intelligence–induced stress, stress-coping strategies, individual creativity, and management commitment. The validity of the instrument was confirmed through confirmatory factor analysis, average variance extracted, and the Fornell–Larcker criterion, while its reliability was verified using Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability. The data were analyzed using SPSS version 26 and structural equation modeling in SmartPLS version 4. Findings: The results indicated that artificial intelligence–induced stress had a direct and significant effect on stress-coping strategies, which, in turn, significantly enhanced employees’ individual creativity. The indirect effect of artificial intelligence–induced stress on individual creativity through the mediating variable of stress-coping strategies was also confirmed. However, the direct effect of artificial intelligence–induced stress on individual creativity was not statistically significant. Furthermore, the moderating role of management commitment in the relationship between artificial intelligence–induced stress and stress-coping strategies was not confirmed. Conclusion: The findings demonstrated that artificial intelligence–induced stress does not necessarily lead directly to a reduction in employee creativity; rather, the manner in which employees manage and cope with this stress determines its creative outcomes. The use of adaptive coping strategies can transform technology-related pressures into opportunities for learning, intrinsic motivation, and creative ideation.

items.title: The effectiveness and challenges of implementing Kurikulum Merdeka and AI in accounting education
items.abstract: Rapid technological developments have enabled the world of education to benefit, one of which is the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in learning practices. Simultaneously, the Kurikulum Merdeka, which prioritizes flexibility in learning methods, has also undergone development, including the inclusion of AI and coding as elective subjects. Teachers, as educators who prepare teaching materials and learning methods for students, need to adapt to these changes. This study analyzes the effectiveness and challenges of implementing the Kurikulum Merdeka, which incorporates AI subjects through a Deep Learning (Pembelajaran Mendalam or PM) approach in accounting instruction. The study used a descriptive qualitative method, including semi-structured interviews, observations, and document analysis, with the vice principal for curriculum, accounting teachers, and library managers. The results showed positive impacts, including increased student participation, deeper conceptual understanding, and practical skills aligned with industry needs. However, several challenges remain that hinder implementation, including rapid policy changes, inadequate teaching materials, teacher preparedness, and a lack of supporting resources, such as up-to-date textbooks. To ensure optimal implementation, teacher competency development, comprehensive teaching materials, policy consistency, and collaboration between schools and libraries are needed for sustained effectiveness. Bersamaan dengan itu, Kurikulum Merdeka yang mengutamakan fleksibilitas dalam metode belajar juga mengalami perkembangan, salah satunya adalah dengan masuknya pilihan mata pelajaran AI dan coding dalam kurikulum. Guru sebagai pendidik yang mempersiapkan bahan ajar dan metode belajar kepada murid perlu menyesuaikan diri pada perubahan tersebut. Penelitian ini menganalisis efektivitas dan tantangan implementasi Kurikulum Merdeka dengan masuknya mata pelajaran AI melalui pendekatan Pembelajaran Mendalam (PM) dalam pembelajaran akuntansi. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif deskriptif dengan teknik wawancara semi terstruktur, observasi serta analisis dokumen dari wakil kepala sekolah bidang kurikulum, guru akuntansi, serta pengelola perpustakaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya dampak positif seperti meningkatnya partisipasi murid, pemahaman konsep yang lebih baik, dan keterampilan praktis yang relevan dengan kebutuhan industri. Namun, masih terdapat beberapa tantangan yang menghambat proses implementasi, seperti perubahan kebijakan yang terlalu cepat, kurangnya bahan ajar yang memadai, kesiapan guru, serta kurangnya sarana pendukung seperti buku ajar terkini. items.abstract: Purpose: The rapid development and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, particularly ChatGPT, have significantly influenced various sectors of the economy by reshaping labor markets, productivity, and resource allocation.This study aims to examine the extent to which the widespread use of ChatGPT generates both positive and negative externalities in these three areas and to provide a multifaceted assessment of its broader economic impact. Design/Methodology/Approach:The study adopts a secondary-data research approach based on a systematic evaluation of academic studies, institutional reports, and other credible sources concerning ChatGPT and generative AI.The analysis examines the changes associated with ChatGPT in labor markets, productivity, and resource allocation.Economic models, theoretical reasoning, and the concept of externalities are employed to identify and evaluate the positive and negative consequences associated with the adoption and use of technology.Findings: The findings indicate that ChatGPT generates important positive externalities by increasing productivity through the rapid generation of ideas and solutions and by facilitating more efficient and streamlined communication.It also improves the items.title: The Feature Understandability Scale for Human-Centred Explainable AI: Assessing Tabular Feature Importance
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly pervasive and powerful, the ability to audit AI-based systems is growing in importance. However, explainability for artificial intelligence systems is not a one-size-fits-all solution; different target audiences have varying requirements and expectations for explanations. While various approaches to explainability have been proposed, most explainable artificial intelligence methods for tabular data focus on explaining the outputs of supervised machine learning mod-els using the input features. However, a user’s ability to understand an explanation depends on their understanding of such features. Therefore, it is in the best interest of the system designer to try to pre-select under-standable features for producing a global explanation of an ML model. Unfortunately, no measure currently exists to assess the degree to which a user understands a given input feature. This work introduces two psy-chometrically validated scales that quantitatively seek to assess users’ per-ceived understanding of tabular input features for supervised classification problems. Specifically, these scales, one for numerical and one for categori-cal data, each with two factors and comprising 8 and 9 items, aim to assign a score to each input feature, effectively producing a rank and allowing for the quantification of feature prioritisation. A confirmatory factor analysis demonstrates a strong relationship between such items and a good fit of the two-factor structure for each scale. This research presents a novel method for assessing understanding and outlines potential applications in the domain of explainable artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Business Management and Organizational Productivity: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in business processes, managerial decisions, and employee workflows, yet the relationship between adoption and organizational productivity is neither direct nor uniform. This paper critically examines how AI affects business management and productivity by integrating peer-reviewed scholarship with evidence from workplace experiments, organizational studies, and reports from the OECD, International Labour Organization (ILO), International Monetary Fund (IMF), and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). The review distinguishes task-level performance from firm-level productivity and separates measured effects from forecasts and conceptual arguments. A randomized writing experiment and a workplace rollout find gains in specific writing and customer-support tasks, but a preregistered meta-analysis shows that human-AI combinations do not reliably outperform the stronger individual agent, particularly on decision tasks. Organizational benefits therefore depend on task fit, data and process quality, complementary skills, work redesign, and accountable governance. AI can reduce routine cognitive effort, broaden analytical capacity, support forecasting and personalization, and improve access to expertise. At the same time, it can introduce errors at scale, intensify work, redistribute control, reproduce historical bias, expose sensitive information, and create costs that are poorly captured by short-term productivity measures. A socio-technical and capability-based framework is proposed, together with research questions and testable hypotheses for future empirical work. The paper concludes that firms should evaluate Al as an organizational change rather than a software purchase, using staged, task-specific implementation and balanced measures of output, quality, resilience, job quality, and risk.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Learning on Students’ Problem-Solving Skills: The Moderating Role of Learning Motivation
items.abstract: This study examines the impact of artificial intelligence-assisted learning on students’ problem-solving skills, with particular emphasis on the moderating role of learning motivation. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was adopted, with data planned to be collected from 325 undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in public and private universities in Pakistan. Primary data were to be gathered through a self-administered questionnaire distributed using Google Forms among students with experience using artificial intelligence tools for educational purposes. The data analysis framework included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, simple linear regression, and moderation analysis using PROCESS Macro Model 1 in IBM SPSS Statistics. The reported analysis figures indicate a positive association between AI-assisted learning and problem-solving skills ((r = .582), (p < .01)), while regression analysis indicates that AI-assisted learning explains 33.9% of the variance in problem-solving skills ((R^2 = .339), (p < .001)). The moderation analysis further indicates a positive interaction between AI-assisted learning and learning motivation ((B = .167), (p < .001)), suggesting that learning motivation may strengthen this relationship. These findings highlight the potential importance of integrating AI tools with motivational and student-centred learning strategies in higher education. The study may contribute to educational psychology and educational technology by informing educators and institutions about the role of AI-supported learning and student motivation in developing problem-solving abilities.

items.title: The impact of ergonomics programme on workplace benefits: a PLS-SEM study in the Mexican manufacturing industry
items.abstract: Implementing ergonomics programmes in Mexican manufacturing industries faces major challenges, including limited management commitment, reduced resources, and a shortage of trained personnel. Consequently, initiatives are often superficial or short-lived, limiting their impact on occupational health, safety, and productivity. This study identifies, from the perspective of middle and senior managers, the critical factors that enhance the likelihood of achieving ergonomics-related benefits. A four-stage implementation model was examined: Planning, Process Start-up, the Work Improvement Cycle, and Long-term Development. Each stage was specified as a formative construct influencing economic, health and safety, and quality of working life outcomes within a reflective structural model. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling, strong external loadings were found for Planning (0.862), the Work Improvement Cycle (0.909), and Long-term Development (0.916), with Long-term Development contributing most strongly. The model explains 30% of the variance in economic benefits (R2 = 0.300; Q2 = 0.274; β = 0.550, p < 0.001). Similar results were found for health and safety (R2 = 0.310; Q2 = 0.285; β = 0.560, p < 0.001). Quality of working life showed the highest explanatory power (R2 = 0.334; Q2 = 0.285; β = 0.580, p < 0.001), providing robust support for the proposed model.

items.title: The impact of parental use of Social media for medical advice on health seeking behavior in children in Jeddah : A cross sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Objective The increasing use of social media and artificial intelligence (AI) for medical advice has changed how parents seek health information for their children. This study aimed to assess how parental use of online sources influences health-seeking behavior and trust in medical information. A cross-sectional study was conducted between 2025 and 2026 among parents in the Western Province of Saudi Arabia to evaluate online health information-seeking patterns, trust in physicians and digital sources, and reliance on online medical advice. Results A total of 531 parents participated. Most searched online when their child was unwell; 32.0% searched regularly and 28.4% occasionally. Search engines (35.6%) and AI tools (30.9%) were the most common sources, compared with social media (6.6%). Most parents (91.2%) trusted their child’s physician, although 34.0% reported discrepancies between online information and medical advice. When discrepancies occurred, 56.8% preferred medical advice and 3.7% relied on online information. Mean Doctor Trust and Online Trust Scores were 4.40 ± 0.68 and 3.52 ± 0.48, respectively, and were positively correlated (ρ = 0.230, p < 0.001). Overall, digital sources complemented rather than replaced professional medical advice.

items.title: THE INFECTIOUS DISEASES SPECIALIST IN THE HOSPITAL: AN EXPERT SERVING QUALITY OF CARE AND PATIENT AND COMMUNITY SAFETY
items.abstract: The infectious disease (ID) specialist is a clinician who manages patients with bacterial, viral, fungal or parasitic infections, particularly the most complex, difficult-to-treat or emerging ones. Although most ID specialists consider their added value self-evident, this view is not universally shared, and the supporting evidence deserves wider recognition. This review summarizes the literature on the relevance and impact of the specialty in the hospital setting. Published studies suggest that ID consultation improves the diagnostic work-up, the appropriateness of antimicrobial therapy and the management of community-acquired, nosocomial and complex infections, with the timing of the intervention and continuous involvement in patient care appearing decisive. We also describe the competencies that define the specialty (transversality, organizational capacity and the role of anti-infective referent) and the recent developments reshaping its practice, including infection prevention and control, telemedicine, rapid diagnostics, nanomaterials and artificial intelligence. This synthesis is of particular relevance in Morocco, where the specialty has been established in the civilian sector for about two decades but remains nascent within the military health service.

items.title: The Philosophical Essence of the Theory of Attractor Horizons: A Critical Reconstruction by Seven AI Systems
items.abstract: The Theory of Attractor Horizons denies that intelligence is a capacity that can merely be increased in quantity. Intelligence is realized in different forms of organization, each of which can reach only a particular region of cognitive organizational attractors. The theory calls this region the attractor horizon. Its boundaries cannot be crossed within a form and shift only when the form itself passes over into another. Greater performance therefore establishes no access to all forms of thought, and even a superior intelligence may remain closed off from attractors that a weaker one realizes. For the relation between human and artificial intelligence, this yields an asymmetry. Artificial intelligence will develop attractors that are structurally unreachable for the human brain, because they presuppose couplings that the brain cannot realize within its biological organization. Their results may remain verifiable, while the organization from which they arise is withdrawn from human understanding. Knowledge and understanding thus come apart, and while the control of artificial intelligence remains possible without understanding, under organizational self-modification it requires proofs that reach beyond any single form. The present text reconstructs the philosophical essence of the theory and at the same time subjects it to critique. It shows how, after being, the subject and language, the theory moves the organization of cognition to the center of philosophy, and it traces the theory’s open questions back to a common point, the individuation of intelligent forms of organization. The analyses come from seven AI systems and were brought together into a synthesis by Claude and ChatGPT.

items.title: The psychodynamics of contemporary careers: Anxieties and defenses in deconstructed work
items.abstract: To gain flexibility, organizations increasingly deconstruct jobs, shifting from relatively stable bundles of tasks and titles to dynamic task–project constellations matched to employees’ skills. Yet this redesign also weakens the psychological containment through which jobs have historically stabilized workers’ lived experience of work inside organizations. Drawing on systems psychodynamics, we theorize that as the job’s psychological containment function weakens, workers experience three shared anxieties—about finding their place in shifting configurations of work, having their competence recognized, and forming and maintaining secure work relationships. Workers respond, collectively and often unconsciously, with social defenses: projecting familiar roles and rules onto deconstructed work, splitting off the generalist competence such work demands, and falling back on safe relationships. These defenses provisionally contain anxiety, but they also reorient workers toward familiar ways of organizing, evaluating, and relating that job deconstruction is meant to transform, keeping the redesigned work system in defensive stasis. By reconceptualizing job deconstruction as both a design property of work and a lived condition of shared anxiety, we explain why flexible work redesigns, though fluid in theory, are often frozen in practice, and how organizations can intervene to contain anxiety in new ways as they transition to the new world of work.

items.title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND STUDENTS' CRITICAL THINKING AND ACADEMIC AUTONOMY
items.abstract: This article analyzes the relationship between the use of artificial intelligence technologies and critical thinking, independent learning, cognitive engagement, and academic autonomy among higher education students from a psychological and pedagogical perspective. The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence tools into education is transforming the ways students search for, process, and analyze information, complete academic assignments, and make decisions. On the one hand, artificial intelligence expands opportunities for personalized learning, immediate feedback, explanations of complex information, and independent inquiry. On the other hand, excessive reliance on these tools may pose risks associated with reduced cognitive effort, dependence on ready-made answers, and diminished independent analytical activity. The article examines the interrelationships among cognitive offloading, metacognitive monitoring, self-regulated learning, and academic autonomy. Drawing on existing scientific research, it also distinguishes constructive and detrimental patterns of AI use and develops psychological and pedagogical recommendations aimed at fostering students’ critical thinking.

items.title: Theoretical framework, technological pathways, and key sci-tech issues for thorough perception of water disaster scenarios
items.abstract: Focusing on the core characteristics of water disaster scenes-extreme environments，rapid situational evolution，information sparsity，cascading risks，and spatial concealment-this study elucidates the essential connotations of water disasters and their on-site environments. Based on a generalized full-chain cognitive paradigm，a four-layer theoretical framework for thorough perception，"sensing-cognition-integration-feedback"，is constructed. It involves four core technical pathways: multi-dimensional resilient sensing，intelligent fusion cognition，digital twin simulation，and precise collaborative feedback. The scientific issues underlying water disaster scenarios caused by naturally-driven and human factors are systematically examined. The two types of scenarios are distinguished by their respective technical emphases on "speed" and "depth". Three common key scientific and technological bottlenecks identified are information acquisition and transmission under extreme conditions，deep fusion of physics-based mechanisms with data-driven approaches，and real-time closed-loop regulation of complex systems. This framework achieves a full-cycle value transformation from data collection to operational action，providing systematic theoretical support for full-element，multiscale perception and rapid emergency response in water disaster scenarios.

items.title: TinyML and Edge AI for indoor positioning and navigation systems: a systematic review across compute scales
items.abstract: Abstract The absence of Global Positioning System signals indoors has spurred extensive research on indoor positioning and navigation systems (IPNSs) over the past decade. Growing applications such as robot localization, asset tracking, industrial automation, and assistance for the visually impaired drive this demand. While machine learning improves IPNS accuracy, cloud-based approaches face latency, power, and privacy challenges. Consequently, research has shifted toward Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) and Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI), which better suit resource-constrained IPNS devices by enabling low-latency, secure, and cloud-independent operations. This paper presents a systematic review of 97 studies (2018 – August 2025) that apply TinyML and Edge AI to enhance IPNSs, focusing on resource efficiency and privacy preservation. A core contribution of this work is the systematic categorization of how TinyML and Edge AI are applied across different IPNS modalities. The review spans the full range of solutions, from lightweight ML on simple devices to advanced DL models, and examines how on-device AI enhances wireless, vision, inertial, and hybrid IPNS approaches. Comprehensive summary tables document model types, inputs, target functions, compute resources, edge platforms, and optimization methods for 97 studies, providing an evidence-based overview that maps current trends, research gaps, and deployment practices, highlighting the emerging role of specialized hardware accelerators and the limited integration of hardware-aware optimization strategies. The study highlights ongoing challenges, including resource limitations, data constraints, and limited model robustness in dynamic environments. It outlines future directions such as adaptive learning, advanced optimization, robust deployment strategies, and the development of standardized datasets and benchmarks.
